Multi-airport architecture.
One connection. Independent airports.

A proposal for configurable airport workflows, shared services, and controllers working across several airports—while preserving each airport’s own operational state.

01

Proposed direction

#

Keep an airport session as the boundary for operational state. Add explicit membership of a EuroScope instance in several airport sessions, independently of its physical WebSocket connection. Load immutable airport definitions from repository configuration and bind compiled workflow handlers with typed settings alongside reusable services. Keep frontend views in code, selected through an airport/view registry, with one selected session per browser tab.

Use one authenticated EuroScope connection with multiplexed, explicitly scoped session messages. Retaining that connection when an instance has no active airport memberships lets coverage changes reattach it automatically. Leaving EKBI must not disconnect EKYT or require an EKDK controller to reconnect the whole plugin.

Keep VATSIM acquisition shared at application scope. Network-data and transceiver feeds each have one fetch/cache pipeline per backend process, consumed by all relevant airport sessions and services. Only airport-specific projections and operational state are session-scoped; adding an airport must not add another upstream poller or full copy of the network snapshot.

PDC is also an application-level shared service. Reuse one transport/client, Hoppie logon key, polling coordinator, and Web PDC integration across enabled airports. Airport definitions select availability and validation; clearance transactions, permissions, and responses remain scoped to their airport/session.

This proposal selects architectural boundaries and a migration direction. Actual airport coverage lists, radio values, master priorities, bay effects, visibility/removal thresholds, and service parameters remain open. Nothing in this document supplies production EKBI, EKYT, or ENGM operating values.

02

Requirements and scope

#

The initial delivery targets EKBI and EKYT using a shared RADIS view/workflow. RADIS has one shared board per airport, no strip or sector ownership, and permits writable non-observer participants working that airport to edit and move strips. The target bay moves and relevant field edits write to EuroScope through the initiating controller's own plugin. Disconnected controllers retain the existing read-only board behavior; their commands must not fall back to the master.

Coverage depends on configured responsibilities and tuned radio frequencies. Mastership is configured independently per airport. EKDK can remain involved when only local tower is present, leave when approach takes over, and rejoin when that coverage returns. A single plugin can be master for several airports and non-master for others.

All existing services should be reusable across airports with the appropriate configuration/data. The EKBI/EKYT delivery uses CDM, stand assignment, and text-pilot support. PDC and AMAN are disabled there, with no planned activation date. Existing EKCH services remain supported. ENGM informs the workflow model but is not added to the first delivery by this proposal.

Configuration lives in the repository and changes may require a restart. Frontend code changes for new airports remain expected. Hot reload, a visual workflow editor, a generic UI renderer, and arbitrary configuration scripts are outside this proposal. Distributed backend election is also outside the initial delivery; existing deployment limits must remain explicit.

03

Existing constraints in the repository

#
Finding Architectural consequence
Sessions already have airport and environment/name fields; strips and controllers reference a session. Preserve that isolation instead of creating a multi-airport session or global shared strip. See session model, session queries, and strip queries.
EuroScope clients hold one session/airport and the plugin has one current role. Split transport identity from membership identity and role. See backend client and plugin WebSocket service.
Frontend association currently looks up one controller by CID; the query uses LIMIT 1. Observer state and disconnect notifications also include CID-wide paths. A multi-session controller requires explicit session and connection binding; changing just the airport field is insufficient. See controller queries and frontend hub.
Airport configuration is loaded into package globals. Bay calculations and stand loading include EKCH constants/paths. Build an airport registry and scope the dependent runtime state, not just the configuration filenames. See config loader, bay helpers, and stand loading.
CDM assembly seeds EKCH; AMAN already has airport-specific terminal definitions and session-aware components. Generalize service assembly while preserving existing domain configuration formats. See application assembly and AMAN terminal configuration.
Coverage already reads primary and transceiver-provider frequencies. Reuse frequency normalization/provider integration, but evaluate participation beyond controllers already in an airport session. See coverage collection.
Application assembly already shares a VATSIM source among SAT, AMAN, and other consumers, and a transceiver cache among radio consumers. Preserve shared acquisition/cache ownership while making consumers airport-aware. The current pilot/prefile snapshot is not a complete controller-staffing inventory. See VATSIM assembly, application wiring, network cache, and transceiver cache.
PDC assembly already builds one service/client from the deployment Hoppie logon; its worker polls LIVE sessions using each airport as the callsign. Preserve shared transport and credentials. Dispatch to airport-aware validation and session-scoped clearance state instead of constructing a PDC client per session. See PDC assembly, client, and service.
Current EuroScope events use protobuf envelopes; frontend events use JSON. Introduce explicit versioning and context without renumbering or reinterpreting existing event payloads. See EuroScope encoding and frontend events.
04

State and identity model

#
Entity Scope and responsibility
Airport definition Immutable combined configuration, bound stateless coded handler, view identifier, service settings, and configuration revision. Shared by sessions for that airport.
Airport session Existing database session ID, airport, and environment/name. Owns strips, board ordering, runway setup, coordinations, and master election. Shared services partition operational records/work by the relevant airport/session; a partition is not a separate client or worker.
Plugin instance One running EuroScope plugin process, identified by an opaque instance ID and authenticated CID. The ID distinguishes connections; it is not authorization by itself.
Plugin connection One authenticated transport, its negotiated capabilities, reported position/radio/environment, and connection generation. Reconnecting invalidates the previous generation.
Membership The instance's attachment to one airport session, with covered responsibilities, observer status, sync readiness, role, and membership generation.
Frontend binding A tab's selected session and the exact compatible own-plugin membership through which it may act.

Retain the current airport plus session-name/environment distinction for LIVE, Sweatbox, and playback. Multi-airport membership must not merge environments or weaken existing exercise/playback identity. A controller's participation in LIVE must not grant access to a same-airport training session. Playback identity remains stable across transport reconnects as in the current plugin.

Do not add a global canonical strip table in this change. The same flight can have independent rows in EKBI and EKYT sessions. Board order, bay, visibility, ownership where enabled, and workflow history remain local to those rows. Flight-plan observations can update both through their authorized feeds; a command never directly copies an airport's bay or order to another airport. Airport-specific runway, stand, and timing semantics also remain local rather than being treated as universally shared flight-plan fields.

RADIS paper-style notes, boolean marks, and timestamp annotations belong to each session strip alongside board order and visibility. Define their types/defaults in the combined workflow configuration and persist/synchronize their values through the backend. Keep this annotation namespace separate from canonical ES flight-plan fields; an annotation does not imply an ES amendment or bypass disconnected read-only behavior. A semantic action can explicitly combine an annotation and ES effect when that mapping is confirmed.

Keep existing controller rows as session-scoped operational projections. A controller observed on the network is not necessarily a connected writable plugin. Use the live membership registry to establish connectivity and command authority; do not derive either from a non-null CID on an arbitrary row.

05

Components and responsibilities

#

The registry resolves static definitions. The membership coordinator determines where an instance participates. Each session runtime owns election, sync, and publication for that session. The bound handler evaluates normalized actions and observations and returns decisions. The shared executor validates them and invokes registered core/domain operations with explicit context. Handlers perform no network/database I/O and own no service clients or workers. Controller command routing targets the initiating controller's exact bound membership regardless of who is master. Automatic work may use the session master or the controller who has assumed the aircraft, through the existing appropriate executor resolution and within that same session (D4). These boundaries can initially be modules in the existing backend; they do not imply new deployed services.

Shared VATSIM sources and PDC transport sit outside airport session runtimes. Coverage and domain services read shared observations and maintain scoped operational projections. The source and PDC diagrams below detail that boundary.

06

Coverage and membership lifecycle

#

Keep coverage separate from strip and sector ownership. A responsibility such as approach can exist in participation policy even when the RADIS board has no sector objects or strip owners.

The backend coordinator evaluates each configured airport from:

  • The instance's declared eligible airports, intersected with enabled airports and server-side participation policy. Configuration of the declaration is a plugin deployment concern; it cannot grant unrestricted access by itself.
  • The instance's environment, primary identity, and current radio frequencies.
  • Configured responsibility matching and fallback, using existing frequency normalization and transceiver integrations where applicable.
  • Current operational staffing, including controllers not running FlightStrips. LIVE staffing/radio evidence must not leak into Sweatbox or playback; those use their own session observations and existing simulation sources.

Evaluate against a shared staffing/radio snapshot, not solely the controller rows in a membership that has already been removed. Otherwise EKDK could not detect when it needs to rejoin. Radio evidence may come from the current providers and plugin reporting; source precedence and freshness handling must be made deterministic in the coordinator, preserving existing matching semantics before extending them. Tuned-frequency coverage must not be inferred from callsign prefixes alone.

The result is a desired set of memberships and covered responsibilities. Apply deltas per airport, without recreating unaffected memberships or resetting their master/sync state. When responsibilities remain, keep the association even if another position takes over a subset. Adding a membership starts its normal initial sync; removing one stops its operational events, master eligibility, and command routing while retaining the physical control connection.

When a replacement such as EKBI_APP takes over all EKDK responsibilities for EKBI, relinquish on its backend attachment or at the configured bounded grace deadline, whichever occurs first. The first delivery may use a near-zero grace policy. Do not require replacement FlightStrips availability indefinitely. Backend attachment and full sync are distinct: relinquishment does not imply the new session data is already ready for writes.

If no ready master remains, use the existing offline/read-only behavior until normal synchronization completes. This is an accepted availability tradeoff, not a reason to keep EKDK attached against the coverage decision. The plugin's intentional startup delay remains; existing constants are not repurposed as an airport grace period. When APP leaves and responsibility returns, membership is restored automatically through the still-connected control path.

For transient transport loss, reuse existing disconnect detection, delay, and reconnect behavior. Control heartbeats must not keep removed airport controller rows, sessions, or service runtimes artificially alive. Session expiry continues to depend on session-scoped operational presence, preserving the current cleanup mechanism and retention interval initially.

07

EuroScope protocol and plugin changes

#

Extend the existing protobuf protocol with explicit multi-airport membership and session context. Deploy backend, frontend, and plugin together while no controllers are online (D5). There is no requirement for concurrent legacy/new protocol support, a second compatibility endpoint, or a single-session client adapter. Reuse existing typed events and add only the context needed for correct session isolation.

The updated connection has two classes of message:

Class Required context Examples
Connection control Authenticated connection and instance; current environment/identity where relevant. Capability negotiation, position/radio updates, eligible-airport declaration, membership list and status changes.
Session traffic Server-issued membership ID/generation, session ID, and the existing typed event payload. Master-produced observations also carry the current master epoch. Initial sync, aircraft/controller changes, runway/SID updates, role metadata, controller commands, and command results.

Wrap existing typed payloads rather than injecting airport fields into every domain message. Exact message names, field numbers, and the wire schema require implementation work; reuse current event types rather than unnecessarily renumbering them. The server binds membership identifiers to the authenticated connection and rejects mismatched, expired, or wrong-environment contexts. Airport text supplied by a client is not sufficient to route a command.

Adapt the current per-session hub/client interfaces to logical membership clients backed by the transport. Existing business handlers should still receive one explicit session context. Any global callsign/CID observer cache, CID-wide disconnect path, sender lookup, and per-client master flag must be audited and replaced where its identity is now membership-specific.

The plugin keeps a membership map rather than one global client_state and master_callsign. Observe EuroScope callbacks once, then dispatch to the appropriate memberships under their roles. Share collected facts where useful; keep per-session sync inventories, exclusion/removal tracking, and role state separate. A full sync for EKBI must not be interpreted as deletion of EKYT data. Coarse observation selection may reduce traffic, but the backend's configured relevance/visibility policy remains authoritative. Automatic inclusion must not depend on a frontend tab being open.

08

Independent master election and synchronization

#

Elect one synchronization master for each airport session, using that airport's configured eligibility and priority. Preserve the current behavior of preferring higher priority clients and retaining the current client on equal priority unless an airport policy explicitly changes that ordering behavior. Observers remain ineligible for mastership. Actual position lists are deferred.

Each election changes a session master epoch. Verify it at message application, not only when a message enters a queue. Late observations or disconnect lists from an old master must not overwrite the replacement's state. Session role messages do not change another membership's role.

A replacement completes the current full-sync/reconciliation process before the session becomes ready. Reuse existing transition protection and delayed aircraft removal where applicable, scoped to the session. Do not treat an incomplete snapshot as authoritative absence. Own-plugin command results remain validatable independently of master role; a non-master must still be able to perform its controller's edits.

Keep election ownership behind a session-scoped interface so it can later use the repository's intended cross-server coordination. Membership IDs and epochs do not by themselves solve distributed election. Initially retain the existing single-authority deployment constraint; do not claim failover between independent backend processes without a shared election/fencing implementation.

09

Frontend session discovery and navigation

#

Replace the singular CID-to-controller lookup with discovery of the current controller's accessible memberships/sessions. Return airport, environment, session ID, view ID, connection readiness, read-only status, and an opaque own plugin binding when available. Derive capabilities and observer state per membership rather than from a CID-wide boolean.

Keep one board session per tab:

  • With no selection and one eligible session, associate directly.
  • With no selection and several eligible sessions, show the initial chooser.
  • With none, preserve the existing no-EuroScope/connection behavior.
  • Preserve a valid explicit tab selection across reconnect. Do not silently switch a disconnected EKBI tab to EKYT just because EKYT remains writable.
  • Use an airport switcher to change this tab; separate tabs keep independent selections and stores. Avoid a global browser storage selection that makes one tab change another.

The server authorizes selection and binds the WebSocket to the chosen session. Reconnect or replace that board subscription on a switch, clear its previous store and pending UI actions, and accept a fresh initial snapshot. Use a subscription generation to reject delayed messages/results from the previous binding. Most JSON payloads can stay session-bound; snapshot and control events must make the binding explicit. Switching or closing tabs does not change the plugin's airport membership or mastership.

An initial snapshot identifies the airport definition revision, coded view, workflow/action IDs, capabilities, and existing session data. Extend the current view registry from EKCH layouts to airport/workflow-specific views; EKBI/EKYT reuse RADIS. Do not deliver an arbitrary UI layout language. Frontend capabilities guide presentation; the backend rechecks authority and workflow conditions for every action.

If the bound own plugin disconnects or loses participation, retain the board with existing read-only behavior even if another plugin is master. Normal reassociation restores editing once that own membership and session are ready. Existing observer restrictions remain in force; RADIS's absence of ownership does not grant observers write access.

RADIS prototype integration baseline

PR #958 provides the likely starting point for the coded RADIS view. The reviewed prototype has four bay IDs (ACTIVE, RUNWAY, PASSIVE_TOP, PASSIVE_BOTTOM), ordering within and between bays, strip menus, FIND/NEW, annotations, and stand interactions. Adapt those components and interactions into the existing application rather than treating the standalone app as a ready multi-controller board. The source review records the pinned revision and limits.

Its browser-local state must become authoritative session state with stable backend strip IDs, revisioned actions, and reconnect snapshots. Its browser VATSIM/ATIS acquisition must use shared backend sources. Preserve useful stand interactions while using the existing airport-aware backend allocator.

The user explicitly identifies feed-only operation without ES updates as a demo shortcut. The target remains own-plugin write-through for real flight changes and configured bay effects, with read-only behavior on disconnect. FIND and NEW also need separate semantics for finding a flight, creating an airport strip, and creating/amending an actual ES flight plan. Prototype thresholds, flight caps, timestamp rules, and extra airport menu entries are not approved operating values or an expansion of initial scope.

NEW is confirmed as creating only a shared airport-local strip for now. Actual ES flight-plan creation is deferred. FIND searches only connected pilots whose flight origin or destination matches the selected airport; prefiles are excluded. D1 now includes all current prototype features, annotation controls (notes, de-icing marks, REA/ATA timestamps), and restoration of manually removed strips. Detailed mappings/recovery values remain airport inputs; PDC/AMAN activation is explicitly excluded by D2.

Read the RADIS prototype review and integration implications

Reviewed on 2026-10-30. Source: FlightStrips PR #958, feat: add FSRADIS prototype as standalone folder, at head commit dba4efc9d4f6d095074c182ebdb50540c7818884. This is a source review of an open prototype PR, not an acceptance of its operating rules or a request to merge it. The user identifies this as the likely basis for further RADIS work and explicitly says the feed-only implementation without EuroScope updates was a demo shortcut.

What the prototype establishes

Observed behavior Consequence for the proposal
Four board containers: ACTIVE, RUNWAY, PASSIVE_TOP, PASSIVE_BOTTOM. Initial departures enter the upper passive area and arrivals the lower one. Dragging supports both inter-bay moves and ordering within a bay. Start the shared RADIS view from these interactions. Preserve distinct bay IDs and authoritative ordering. Production placement and movement effects still need airport configuration.
Strip menus cover route/heading, altitude, flight plan, runway, and numeric cells. Other interactions include SID, RNAV, VFR, remarks, REA/ATA timestamps, and a de-icing flag. Translate UI interactions into semantic backend actions. Separate real flight-plan/ES fields from shared paper-style annotations; screen cell names such as U2/B5 are presentation details.
FIND searches feed pilots outside the normal distance filter; selecting a result adds it to a passive area. NEW creates a local strip, with callsign lookup and manual entry. Distinguish finding an existing flight, creating an airport strip, and creating or amending an actual ES flight plan. A local strip alone does not establish an ES flight plan. Define identity and admission semantics before wiring these actions.
Deleting a feed strip hides its callsign locally. Manual/planned strips are removed from local maps. Refresh merges feed records while preserving existing bay membership/order and local strips. Use session-owned visibility/removal and recovery rules. A refresh or another browser must not undo a shared deletion. Do not delete the canonical flight merely because its airport strip is removed.
Stand data are parsed from a GRplugin-style file. Assignment considers sensed position, aircraft/stand criteria, occupancy, and manual overrides. Reuse the existing backend stand-assignment service and airport data. Retain the useful UI behavior; avoid two independent allocators deciding the same airport's stands.
Airport selection changes the displayed board; the menu contains EKYT, EKBI, EKAH, EKSP, and EKKA. Selection is saved in browser storage. Adapt this to authorized session discovery and per-tab selection. Menu entries are demo evidence, not approval to add three more airports to the first release.

Evidence: App.tsx, CommandDialogs.tsx, standAssignment.ts.

Prototype boundaries that must change during integration

  • Board state, annotations, locks, hidden callsigns, and stand overrides live in browser memory. They do not provide the required shared board, persistence, reconnect snapshot, authorization, or concurrent editing across controllers.
  • App.tsx polls the VATSIM pilot feed in the browser; CommandBar.tsx separately polls it for ATIS/runway information and obtains weather. Integrated views consume backend observations and shared source caches. Airport sessions and browser tabs must not create independent VATSIM feed acquisition loops.
  • There is no ES write path. Actual flight changes and configured bay effects must use the initiating controller's own plugin, with edits blocked when that binding is unavailable. Read-only behavior applies to board annotations too, following the agreed whole-board disconnect policy.
  • Generated array-position strip IDs and browser-only manual IDs are unsuitable as shared identities. Use backend flight identity plus independent session strip IDs, with idempotent creation/admission and revisioned mutations.
  • The standalone React application must be adapted to the host view registry, session store, WebSocket, design conventions, and dependency versions. Keeping its visual interaction model does not require shipping a second application.

Evidence: prototype README, App.tsx, CommandBar.tsx.

Values and semantics that remain unapproved

The demo uses a 150 NM filter, a ten-flight cap (also affecting FIND), 15-second feed polling, a 14,000 ft admission filter for newly encountered departures, and a 500 ft timestamp threshold. It estimates some timing from a fixed 15-minute taxi value. None is adopted as an operational default. The feed lookup reads pilots, not prefiles, so its "planned" results do not establish prefile support. Its REA toggle changes a local timestamp; it does not demonstrate an EOBT update. Fallback weather, fixed cells, sample SID/runway logic, and button labels do not prove working CDM, AMAN, PDC, or complete flight-plan amendment support.

Airport-specific admission/removal thresholds, bay-to-ES mappings, timestamp meaning, manual-strip data/flight association, runway/ATIS authority, and service parameters remain open. Existing confirmed ownership, coverage, own-plugin, and disconnect requirements take precedence over demo behavior.

Confirmed feature scope — 2026-11-01

Include all current prototype features, notes/de-icing/REA/ATA annotations, and restoration of manually removed strips. NEW is local-strip creation only; FIND is restricted to connected pilots to/from the selected airport, with no prefiles. Use the existing EKCH execution/error/reconciliation flow. PDC and AMAN remain disabled at EKBI/EKYT without a scheduled activation date. The demo shortcuts above still do not become target architecture or approved airport constants.

Resulting architecture changes

Use PR #958 as the likely RADIS frontend starting point. Keep shared observations outside airport runtimes, then project them into each airport's admission rules. Store strip order, visibility, annotations, and overrides in the authoritative session. Send semantic actions from the adapted view to backend workflow/domain handlers; send real ES changes through the initiating plugin and reconcile their observations. Never treat a successful local UI mutation as proof of an ES write.

The coded-handler proof now exercises a typed shared boolean annotation in the fictional airport config. RADIS text, marks, and timestamp annotations remain shared strip data distinct from canonical ES fields, but their complete declarations and semantics must be defined with the real RADIS handler. The fictional example is not a RADIS spec.

Integration acceptance must include two controllers seeing the same mutations, stable strip identity across reordered feed snapshots, reconnect convergence, own-plugin write routing, and no browser/per-session VATSIM acquisition loops.

10

Repository configuration and workflow model

#

Use one combined, versioned configuration file per airport. It contains geography, positions, coverage, master policy, ownership, routes, coded view selection, handler selection/settings, bays, services, and validation. Large reference files such as stand data and AMAN terminals remain referenced domain assets. There is no separate workflow-profile file or general rule interpreter.

Load and validate these files at startup, select a registered handler, and build an immutable airport definition. Bind it to each session once. Controllers' events call the already selected implementation directly; they do not parse configuration, load files, or scan handlers. Reuse one stateless implementation across definitions where appropriate, with all mutable state kept in sessions.

Production activation must use an explicit deployment selection of files; neither presence in the repository nor the fictional example activates an airport. E1 covers atomic validation/failure policy and the production loader.

Configuration coverage and coded workflow handlers

The selected direction is coded workflow handlers with typed configuration. EKBI/EKYT can share RADIS with separate airport values, EKCH retains its own implementation, and ENGM can add a different implementation when required. Custom features are normal code. Add shared settings/operations when behavior is reusable; do not expand a configuration language to represent each exception.

Boundary Responsibility
Airport configuration Geography, positions/frequencies, coverage and master values, service selection/data, bays, annotation declarations, and typed handler settings such as supported mappings and lifecycle thresholds.
Workflow handler Decisions for semantic actions, observation reconciliation, lifecycle, coordination, and custom airport features. It interprets its validated settings and returns data describing state changes/effect intents.
Shared application core Session isolation, authentication, observer/readiness checks, configured ownership enforcement, revisions/concurrency, persistence/broadcasts, decision validation, shared feeds, and own-plugin ES routing.
Reusable services and views CDM, stand assignment, AMAN, and other domain algorithms keep their implementations. Coded views use explicit session/action contracts.

Select one workflow implementation per airport definition from a compiled registry. Inject immutable typed settings and read-only decision context. Keep narrow hooks for controller actions, normalized observations, lifecycle evaluation, and coordination as required. Establish one explicit handler for each event; avoid competing generic/EKCH/airport handler chains or implicit fallbacks. A handler cannot bypass core authority, concurrency, or command-routing rules.

Handlers return typed service-operation intents; the executor calls the shared service and normalizes its result for further decisions. Network I/O must not occur while holding strip/session locks or database transactions. The sample's two-command core allowlist and boolean-only annotations demonstrate a bounded proof, not the final extensible action catalog or complete RADIS data model. Register supported action descriptors with each production handler (E2).

Each registered ID owns a concrete settings schema and Go settings type. Unknown IDs/settings, unsupported actions, invalid bay references, and incompatible ownership or service dependencies are errors. This is repository code, not runtime scripts or an untyped settings bag. A new implementation needs a factory, typed settings/schema branch, action contract, and behavioral tests.

Concrete combined configuration and examples

The JSON Schema now defines a single airport document with closed typed objects and handler-specific settings. The schema contract defines field semantics, units, references, and migration evidence. The earlier declarative profile/override format has been superseded; its separate example profile files have been removed.

The EKCH example includes all 18 bays and selects its coded handler in the same file:

workflow:
  handler: ekch/v1
  settings:
    airborne_altitude_agl_ft: 200
    relevant_distance_nm: 30
  bays:
    # The complete file lists all 18 existing EKCH bays.
    - {id: TAXI, label: TAXI}
    - {id: DEPART, label: DEPART}

This excerpt is not a standalone config. The complete file preserves every one of the current YAML's 20 top-level settings: 25 positions, 21 sector variants, 33 ground routes, two airborne SID families, and 19 layout mappings. The validator reconstructs the parsed original exactly and checks the code-derived master priorities, elevation, and distance. Lifecycle thresholds are now handler settings rather than a separate adapter/profile file.

The fictional ZZZZ example is a complete second combined file with invented values, no ownership, disabled services, and an example-paper/v1 handler. Its concrete settings are:

settings:
  initial_bay: HOLD
  runway_bay: RUNWAY
  bay_ground_states:
    HOLD: TAXI
    RUNWAY: LINEUP
    DONE: PARK
  ground_state_bays:
    TAXI: HOLD
    LINEUP: RUNWAY

The full file declares HOLD/RUNWAY/DONE and a typed review_required boolean annotation. Moving into RUNWAY sets the mark; the handler's custom review.clear action clears it. The configuration selects values; the custom action is code. ZZZZ is demonstration data, not a real rollout target or a RADIS specification. Actual EKBI/EKYT/ENGM values remain open.

Executable handler proof and its limits

The handler design and reproduction guide describes the runnable example in the Go package and demo command. It loads both combined files simultaneously, binds different handlers, and demonstrates session-local state and own-plugin command intents. Tests also cover independent sessions sharing one handler/definition, definitions sharing code with different settings, stale revisions, invalid decisions, observer/readiness/ownership checks, and snapshot isolation. Race checks and dispatch benchmarks are included.

The EKCH handler wraps the actual shared.GetDepartureBay and shared.GetGroundState functions. It preserves their lower/tower taxi-bay and forward-only departure behavior in the tested paths. This demonstrates real code reuse, not full declarative coverage. Those helpers still contain EKCH geography/distance constants; the adapter rejects incompatible values until that code is made airport-aware. The airborne threshold is supplied from settings.

The example does not activate either airport in application startup. Its Go loader consumes the workflow projection; full domain/resource validation runs through the schema tool. Its executor is in memory and emits inspectable command intents, not ES acknowledgements. Production authentication, membership epochs, transactions, transport, services, incremental observations, admission/removal, and coordination including EKCH SQ rules still require integration. No full EKCH runtime-parity claim follows from these examples.

The sample immediately changes its in-memory bay before returning an outbound intent. It does not implement the full production move/error/observation path or admission; D3 selects reuse of existing EKCH execution, not a new pending framework or ES-confirmation gate. Its callsign-keyed store is also not proof of stable flight/strip identity across callsign reuse or manual creation (E3).

ENGM requires bay placement and clearance state to be separate: dragging a departure into the runway line can mean lineup, while another semantic action enters the same line with takeoff clearance. Its coded handler can return these different decisions for the same destination bay, with typed target/mode data as needed. Pending handoff and external acceptance remain distinct events. These requirements constrain the handler/core contract without requiring a generic rule interpreter or complete ENGM implementation in the first RADIS release. The draft ENGM SUP role remains distinct from synchronization mastership.

RADIS disables strip/sector ownership while coverage responsibilities still govern participation. Its notes/marks/timestamps must be typed shared strip state, separate from actual ES fields. The fictional proof exercises a boolean annotation; concrete RADIS text/timestamp declarations and semantics remain implementation/airport inputs. Disconnected read-only behavior applies to those actions too.

Validate handler IDs/settings, bay/action references, dependencies, coded view compatibility, and required resources before activation. Reject invalid airports without falling back to EKCH. Services retain their existing readiness behavior; it is distinct from structurally invalid configuration.

Read the handler design, proof, and reproduction commands

Status: selected direction for the architecture draft, with an isolated Go example. This is not application activation or a complete EKCH migration.

The consistency review and planning register separates the D1–D5 decisions confirmed on 2026-11-01, proportionate engineering work (E1–E7), and airport rollout inputs. The user selected existing EKCH execution and a coordinated offline upgrade; the proof does not establish full runtime parity.

Boundaries and dispatch

Use one combined airport YAML file. It selects a registered workflow handler and contains that handler's concrete typed settings, bays, and declared annotations, alongside coverage, master policy, ownership, views, services, and validation. Large domain datasets may remain referenced files. There is no separate workflow profile, inherited rule list, embedded script, or generic interpreter.

At startup, validate the full document and resource references, resolve the registered implementation, decode/validate its settings, and construct an immutable definition. Select that definition when creating a session. Every event then calls the already bound handler directly. No per-event config decoding, file access, registry scan, handler discovery, or airport conditionals are required in the common dispatcher.

Part Owns
Airport definition Immutable settings, handler instance, known bays/annotations, service dependencies, and revision.
Handler Workflow decisions for typed actions and observations. It is stateless and can be shared by all sessions using the definition.
Session/core Mutable strip state, isolation, synchronization, revisions, permissions, persistence/broadcasts, and execution of validated effects; shared services may own session-keyed partitions without separate clients/workers per session.
Services Existing CDM/stand/AMAN algorithms with explicit scoped dependencies; shared VATSIM acquisition stays outside handlers and sessions.

PDC is an application-level shared service too: one provider client, transport, polling coordinator, and deployment logon serve all enabled airports. A handler requests operations through the core with explicit airport/session context; it does not own a PDC client or credentials. Airport validation and clearance/timeout state remain scoped. The isolated handler example does not instantiate external services.

Production hooks should cover controller actions, normalized observations, admission/lifecycle evaluation, and coordination where required. The executable proof implements only bay movement, full-flight observations, and one custom action. Those hooks are small enough to exercise the boundary without claiming the rest of the application has been migrated.

The handler receives a session snapshot and a typed event and returns a decision containing state changes and effect intents. It cannot access the database, transport, VATSIM feed, or a mutable current-airport global. The common executor checks the complete decision before applying any changes. The production executor must add transactional persistence, broadcasts, and reliable dispatch; an emitted ES intent is not an acknowledgement.

Production domain-service requests are typed intents executed by the core; handlers do not synchronously invoke service I/O. Normalize service results back into decision inputs and release session/strip locks or database transactions before network calls. Human deferred actions retain their own-plugin authority; D4 permits genuine automatic effects through the same session master or the controller who has assumed the aircraft, using the existing suitable resolver. Human-originated work retains its own plugin. PDC and AMAN stay disabled at EKBI/EKYT, while current EKCH services are preserved.

Use one explicit owner for each event. Avoid chains of generic, EKCH, and airport fallback handlers. Share helpers or a whole workflow implementation where behavior matches: EKBI/EKYT can share RADIS, while retaining separate definitions and session state. A distinct feature can be implemented in a dedicated handler without adding a configuration language construct or branching throughout the shared services.

Concrete implementations in the proof

The opt-in handler proof patch contains the example package, handlers, in-memory executor, tests, and demo command. It is a specification artifact; application files are not added by this spec PR.

Config and handler Demonstrated behavior
EKCH, ekch/v1 Wraps the actual shared.GetDepartureBay and shared.GetGroundState functions. A TAXI observation selects TAXI or TAXI_LWR depending on ground staffing. Moving to DEPART produces a LINEUP intent. Existing specific taxi placement and forward-only departure behavior remain delegated to the real helper.
Fictional ZZZZ, example-paper/v1 A first TAXI observation selects HOLD. Later observations preserve manual board placement. Moving to RUNWAY emits the configured LINEUP intent and sets a shared review_required flag. The coded review.clear action clears that flag only in the runway bay; it is not supported by EKCH.

ZZZZ, its geography, frequencies, thresholds, and operating values are invented demonstration data. It is not an airport to deploy and does not establish RADIS requirements. It has no ownership and disables all services. No coded frontend for this fictional view is included.

EKCH's combined example preserves all 20 existing YAML settings, all 18 bays, and selected code-derived values. Its helper still contains geography/distance constants: the example adapter explicitly rejects different values rather than claiming the helper is fully configurable. Its positive airborne threshold is passed from typed settings into the existing function.

Configuration and extension contract

workflow.handler is a versioned registered ID. Each implementation has a closed settings object selected by JSON Schema oneOf and a corresponding Go settings type decoded with unknown-field rejection. Unknown IDs/settings, invalid references, incompatible ownership, and unsupported annotations fail validation. The current registry and schema define exactly ekch/v1 and example-paper/v1.

Adding a real implementation requires its typed settings/schema branch, factory registration, handler code, supported action contract, and behavioral tests. Changing only airport values uses the same implementation without adding code. Compiled handlers do not mean a separate copy of the shared backend per airport.

The sample executor still has an explicit allowlist for strip.move and review.clear. A production dispatcher must obtain supported typed action descriptors from handler registration, rather than add each custom action to the common core. Likewise, the sample's callsign-keyed in-memory storage is not the production identity contract for reused callsigns or manual strips (E2/E3).

Annotations belong to session strips. This proof exercises one declared boolean flag, not a general implementation of every RADIS text/timestamp field. Future RADIS settings must concretely declare those fields and their types. Actual ES fields remain distinct. The shared whole-board read-only policy also applies to annotation-only actions.

Isolation, correctness, and performance checks

The example constructs EKCH and ZZZZ simultaneously from their complete combined files and also exercises two sessions sharing one definition and two airport definitions sharing the paper implementation with different settings. Tests use the same callsign across sessions, concurrent conflicting edits, and independent observations. Returned snapshots do not alias stored state.

Shared guards reject observer/disconnected/wrong-session edits, missing own plugin binding, stale revisions, unknown bays, configured ownership violations, invalid handler decisions, and observation-to-ES write loops. The executor supplies the outbound plugin identity; the handler cannot choose another sender or request master fallback. Binding and observation inputs in this proof are trusted test/core inputs; production authentication and membership-generation validation remain integration work.

One mutex protects each sample session. Different sessions do not share a lock; immutable handler/config state requires no event-path lock. This is an example of serialization boundaries, not a replacement decision for the current database transaction model. Tests run under the Go race detector. Benchmarks measure the complete in-memory session execution path, including guards, snapshots, and result construction; they exclude YAML loading and do not establish production latency or an end-to-end throughput guarantee.

A local Windows/amd64 run on 2026-10-30 (Go 1.26.0, Ryzen 7 7700X) measured:

In-memory command path Time/op Allocated bytes/op Allocations/op
EKCH 256.2 ns 272 8
Fictional paper workflow 633.9 ns 1,152 13

These are single-run development measurements of the whole sample executor, not a before/after production comparison or an operational latency target.

To run the isolated proof from a clean spec checkout, first apply its optional artifact from the repository root. This creates demonstration files under backend locally; it does not wire them into application startup:

git apply --check .github/specs/multi-airport-support/examples/handler-proof.patch
git apply .github/specs/multi-airport-support/examples/handler-proof.patch
cd backend

Then run from backend:

go test -race ./internal/airportworkflow ./internal/shared
go test ./internal/airportworkflow -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkSessionDispatch -benchmem
go run ./cmd/workflow-example ../.github/specs/multi-airport-support/examples/ekch.airport.yaml ../.github/specs/multi-airport-support/examples/zzzz.airport.yaml

The command prints both decisions, own-plugin command intents, and a blocked disconnected edit. It starts no application services and performs no network or database writes. Validate the full document/reference contract separately using the schema tool, as described in the schema contract.

What remains before real integration

Application startup still loads the existing EKCH YAML. No application route, WebSocket, protocol, database, membership, or service assembly has been replaced. The example loader reads/validates the workflow projection of the combined file; unconsumed domain blocks are YAML nodes and are validated by the full schema tool, not by a claimed complete production Go loader.

The sample immediately commits an in-memory move and returns an outbound intent; it has no durable pending state, request deduplication, or ES acknowledgement protocol. D3 selects reuse of the existing EKCH production execution/error path, not a new confirmation gate or durable pending-move framework. Its trusted binding, per-session mutex, and side-effect return values are evidence of the boundary only, not a substitute for authenticated epochs, database transactions, or reliable dispatch. The example is not a background-service executor.

Incremental ground-state/position messages, admission/removal/recovery, coordination including EKCH SQ behavior, other field edits, CDM/stand/text-pilot integration, and frontend actions still need adaptation. Preserve existing EKCH PDC/AMAN; activation at EKBI/EKYT is deferred without a date. Backend/frontend/ plugin will be upgraded together while nobody is online, with no parallel legacy protocol or extended support-window work. The tested EKCH paths delegate to real functions; this is not proof that every existing path has moved behind the interface or that full runtime parity is established.

Inspect the actual sample Go handlers
package airportworkflow

import (
	"fmt"

	"FlightStrips/internal/database"
	"FlightStrips/internal/shared"
	"FlightStrips/pkg/events/euroscope"
)

const (
	Move        = "strip.move"
	ClearReview = "review.clear"
	observe     = "flight.observed"
)

type event struct {
	kind         string
	bay          string
	flight       *euroscope.Strip
	groundOnline bool
}

// A decision contains data only. A handler has no database, transport, shared
// feed, goroutine, or mutable current-airport dependency.
type decision struct {
	bay         string
	groundState *string
	annotations map[string]bool
}

type handler interface {
	decide(Strip, event) (decision, error)
}

type ekchHandler struct {
	airport  string
	settings ekchSettings
}

func (h ekchHandler) decide(strip Strip, event event) (decision, error) {
	switch event.kind {
	case Move:
		result := decision{bay: event.bay}
		if state := shared.GetGroundState(event.bay); state != euroscope.GroundStateUnknown {
			result.groundState = &state
		}
		return result, nil
	case observe:
		var existing *database.Strip
		if strip.Revision != 0 {
			existing = &database.Strip{Origin: strip.Origin, Destination: strip.Destination, Bay: strip.Bay, State: strip.State}
		}
		return decision{bay: shared.GetDepartureBay(*event.flight, existing, h.settings.AirborneAltitude, h.airport, event.groundOnline)}, nil
	default:
		return decision{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported EKCH action %q", event.kind)
	}
}

// This is a fictional workflow, not a RADIS operational specification. Its
// custom review feature is ordinary code, with no new rule-language operation.
type paperHandler struct{ settings paperSettings }

func (h paperHandler) decide(strip Strip, event event) (decision, error) {
	switch event.kind {
	case Move:
		result := decision{bay: event.bay}
		if state, ok := h.settings.BayGroundStates[event.bay]; ok {
			result.groundState = &state
		}
		if event.bay == h.settings.RunwayBay {
			result.annotations = map[string]bool{"review_required": true}
		}
		return result, nil
	case ClearReview:
		if strip.Bay != h.settings.RunwayBay {
			return decision{}, fmt.Errorf("review can only be cleared in runway bay")
		}
		return decision{bay: strip.Bay, annotations: map[string]bool{"review_required": false}}, nil
	case observe:
		// The paper workflow preserves manual placement on later observations.
		if strip.Revision != 0 {
			return decision{bay: strip.Bay}, nil
		}
		bay, ok := h.settings.GroundStateBays[event.flight.GroundState]
		if !ok {
			bay = h.settings.InitialBay
		}
		return decision{bay: bay}, nil
	default:
		return decision{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported paper action %q", event.kind)
	}
}

func knownGroundState(state string) bool {
	switch state {
	case "", "ST-UP", "PUSH", "TAXI", "LINEUP", "DEPA", "PARK":
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

Read the complete configuration schema contract

Status: concrete combined-file contract for coded workflow handlers, with two validated examples and an executable isolated Go proof. Application startup has not been migrated. This draft replaces the earlier profile/rule-language design.

See the planning register for D1–D5, confirmed by the user on 2026-11-01. Follow existing EKCH execution; allow genuine automatic effects through the same session master or assuming controller; deploy together while nobody is online. PDC/AMAN remain disabled at EKBI/EKYT. The schema and fictional proof do not themselves implement these production behaviors.

Artifacts and strictness

  • JSON Schema: Draft 2020-12, 37 reachable typed definitions, one root airport document.
  • Complete EKCH file: all current settings plus handler selection, settings, and bays, without a separate workflow profile.
  • Fictional ZZZZ file: concrete second airport using a different handler, no ownership, and disabled services. Never deploy it.
  • Executable proof and commands: actual Go handlers, per-session executor, tests, race checks, and dispatch benchmarks.
  • Validator and report: structural/reference/handler checks and lossless EKCH reconstruction.

All objects are closed unless explicitly typed maps; unknown properties and null placeholders are errors. The root requires kind: airport, schema_version: flightstrips-airport/v1, and a four-uppercase-letter airport. Frequencies remain strings. Paths are repository-relative and cannot escape the repository. Duplicate YAML keys and stable IDs are rejected.

One airport file combines the operational configuration. Large service datasets remain referenced assets; they are not copied into every YAML document. No application-scoped VATSIM fetch/cache configuration belongs in an airport file. The current application still loads backend/config/ekch.yaml.

Airport fields

Field Contract
$schema Optional editor hint pointing to the schema file.
schema_version, kind, airport Required document identity.
geography Required latitude/longitude/elevation, transition altitude, declared runways, runway initial-CFL map, and an optional region-file resource (required when a coverage rule names a region). Values carry explicit units in their names.
positions Position name, string frequency, and section; names must be unique.
coverage.matching Primary-frequency matching, tuned-frequency participation, callsign fallback, and registered normalization/provider-selection strategy. v1 uses the existing VATSIM normalization and coverage algorithm.
coverage.responsibilities Rules with stable IDs, logical name/optional key, optional display/region/runway/direction constraints, name priority, and ordered providers. Variant rules may share a logical responsibility but cannot share a rule ID.
coverage.airborne_fallback Ordered configured positions providing the existing airborne fallback.
coverage.membership Either legacy-single-airport/v1, preserving today's association while migrating EKCH, or remaining-responsibilities/v1 with a nonnegative relinquish_grace_seconds. The latter supports the agreed automatic leave/rejoin policy. The legacy label preserves EKCH association semantics; it does not require support for an old client protocol.
master Ordered position/matching rules, higher-priority preemption flag, equal-priority policy, fallback policy, and an explicit false observer-eligibility value.
ownership Independent strip mode (none/route) and sector mode (none/coverage), plus eligible callsign prefixes. Coverage does not require ownership to exist.
routing Stable-ID ground routes, airborne SID families/default, and runway-to-position missed-approach mapping. Ground routes retain the current typed runway/stand selectors, path, active-runway conditions, and owner overrides.
view A coded view ID, existing position/staffing/runway layout variants, airborne fallback layout, and message-area recipients. The ordered layout list keeps the existing last-matching-variant semantics.
workflow Registered handler ID, closed handler-specific settings, complete bay catalog, and handler-supported typed annotation declarations in this same file.
services A closed map of reusable services. Each entry declares availability and the service's typed config/data dependencies when active or deployment-managed.
validation Typed clearance and taxiway validation definitions, preserving current domain formats. PDC-specific validation belongs to its service entry.
provenance Source paths and normalized-LF SHA-256 fingerprints for this worked migration. These are audit metadata, not executable imports or authorization.

Numeric runway selectors and numeric stand identifiers are accepted where the existing YAML uses them. Resolution stringifies selectors in the same way as the current loader; new authored runway strings should be quoted. Supporting those typed scalar alternatives allows the example to reconstruct the original parsed YAML exactly, not just drop values that are inconvenient for a new shape.

All repository resource paths are relative to the repository root, not the including file. repo_path cannot escape the repository. A resource can instead name an environment variable and a default repository path for runtime-installed data. The ignored ICAO aircraft database is represented that way: validation does not falsely claim the deployment asset exists in Git. Credentials and external-service logon secrets remain deployment concerns.

For region files, semantic validation must read the selected resource to check coverage region names. A nonblank environment override takes precedence; unset or blank values use default_repo_path. Absolute environment paths may reference deployment files outside the repository; relative overrides resolve from the repository root. Repository paths/defaults remain constrained to the repository. A missing selected region file is a validation error, not a fallback to another file or a KeyError.

Reusable service entries

availability is one of enabled, disabled, or deployment:

  • enabled requests the capability at this airport, subject to deployment support, required credentials, and service readiness.
  • disabled disables it at this airport; its data fields are not required.
  • deployment preserves the current environment/application enable flag during migration. It does not assert that the service is currently running.

The EKCH example uses deployment rather than guessing the current flags. This preserves EKCH activation; it does not turn PDC/AMAN on for EKBI/EKYT, where both are explicitly disabled. There is no committed regional activation date. Disabled services still reject unknown properties. An unavailable dependency must follow the service's existing readiness behavior; it must not load EKCH data as a fallback for another airport.

Service Typed configuration/data
cdm config_root and the complete current CDM config: rates, LVO rate, rate/SID-interval/taxizone URIs, default taxi time, and deice durations/platforms. Existing domain field names are preserved. Relative CDM data URIs resolve below config_root; HTTP(S) URIs remain external resources.
stand_assignment Stand, aircraft-reference, ICAO aircraft, airline-assignment, and scenery resources. The ICAO resource may use the existing environment override. Mutable assignments/reservations remain session state.
text_pilot Registered frequency-message/v1 transport/provider and coded layout-data resource. This reuses the transport; airport-specific UI/phrase behavior still needs its view/workflow code.
aman Existing versioned terminal and boundary resources. Its own configuration format/validation remains authoritative rather than being flattened into generic transition settings.
pdc Availability and current heavy-aircraft/runway and SID/engine validation settings. The service, provider client, transport, polling coordinator, and deployment HOPPIE_LOGON are shared across enabled airports. Mailbox identity and clearance state remain airport/session-aware. No airport-local credential or poller fields are accepted.
ecfmp Per-airport availability; the shared external client remains configured at deployment scope.

There is deliberately no vatsim service or poller entry under an airport. Shared acquisition/cache configuration remains application-scoped. Airport rules consume snapshots and produce scoped operational results.

Likewise, PDC credentials are configured once at deployment scope, not copied into each airport file. The existing provider client accepts a separate airport callsign for sends/polls using the same logon. No shared-service selector is needed: every enabled services.pdc entry uses the application PDC service. Removing/adding that entry must not create or destroy a separate transport.

Coded workflow settings

workflow is a closed oneOf keyed by handler, with exactly two registered branches in this proof. There is no dynamic script, arbitrary factory name, untyped property bag, rule interpreter, or implicit fallback.

Handler Required settings and constraints
ekch/v1 airborne_altitude_agl_ft: positive integer; relevant_distance_nm: positive number. A nonempty bays list contains every existing EKCH bay ID/label. No annotation block is accepted. The adapter requires airport EKCH, existing route/coverage ownership, and the helper's legacy geography/distance.
example-paper/v1 initial_bay, runway_bay: distinct known bay IDs; bay_ground_states: map of known bay IDs to ES ground-state enums; ground_state_bays: reverse map to known bay IDs. bays contains unique IDs/labels. annotations.review_required is required and closed with type: boolean, scope: session, default: false. Ownership must be disabled.

Ground-state values are '', ST-UP, PUSH, TAXI, LINEUP, DEPA, and PARK. A mapping is configuration interpreted by handler code; absence of an outgoing mapping means no ES ground-state intent. The example paper handler uses incoming mappings only for first placement and preserves later manual placement. Its coded review.clear feature has no counterpart in EKCH.

The boolean annotation is stored per strip in its airport session. It is not a browser value, one global board flag, or a canonical ES field. Its changes use ordinary revisioned core actions and follow observer/readiness rules. This concrete example does not claim to define the full RADIS annotation catalog.

For another implementation, add its closed schema branch, corresponding typed Go settings, registered factory, action contract, and tests. Same behavior with different values reuses a handler. A new airport-specific behavior can be code without expanding a universal workflow language. Admission/removal thresholds belong in the settings of the handler implementing that lifecycle; no separate lifecycle adapter document is required.

The full Python validator checks all domain sections and repository references. The isolated Go loader strictly decodes the workflow and required context; other domain blocks are retained as YAML nodes and not installed into existing singletons. Production startup must compose these domain validators rather than mistake this example projection for a full application loader.

Full-file validation, strict workflow decoding, and runtime activation are separate steps. Production must compose the domain validators and ensure parity with the authored schema (E1), including required fields, all legacy bays, and supported coded views. The example Go loader is not itself proof of that parity. Airport files are selected explicitly for deployment; examples are not discovered and activated automatically. The sample's fixed command catalog and boolean annotation support do not imply a completed production action/data contract (E2).

EKCH mapping and evidence

All 20 top-level settings from the current YAML are reconstructed by the validator and compared with the original parsed YAML, including the ordering of arrays. Comments, numeric spelling, anchors, and whitespace are not runtime settings and are not compared byte-for-byte.

Existing setting(s) New location
latitude, longitude geography.latitude, geography.longitude
transition_altitude, runway_initial_cfl, runways geography.transition_altitude_ft, geography.initial_cfl_ft, geography.runways
positions positions unchanged
sectors coverage.responsibilities; add stable rule IDs and rename owner to providers, retaining all other fields/order. ownership.sectors: coverage selects the compatibility projection.
owner_callsign_prefixes ownership.callsign_prefixes
airborne_owners coverage.airborne_fallback
airborne_fallback_layout, layouts, message_areas Corresponding view fields
routes routing.ground, with added stable IDs; all selectors, paths, active conditions, and overrides retained
airborne_routes, missed_approach_handover routing.airborne, routing.missed_approach
airborne_altitude_agl workflow.settings.airborne_altitude_agl_ft
cdm services.cdm.config unchanged
pdc_validation services.pdc.validation unchanged
clx_validation, taxiway_type_validation validation.clearance, validation.taxiway_types unchanged

The example contains 25 positions, 21 sector variants, 33 ground routes, two airborne SID families, and 19 position-layout mappings. The same combined file contains all 18 bay constants. Code-derived values are the five-position master priority, elevation of 17 ft, and relevance distance of 30 NM. Their source fingerprints are included so stale examples are detected on revalidation.

This validates representability and a lossless settings migration. It does not prove full runtime behavior equivalence: automatic bay reconciliation, service lifecycles, frontend actions, and commands still need handler/core integration and controlled integration checks in the implementation work. Existing backend configuration, service flags, and deployment behavior are unchanged by this example.

Reproduce the checks

From the repository root:

python -m pip install -r .github/specs/multi-airport-support/schema/requirements.txt
python .github/specs/multi-airport-support/schema/validate_examples.py --write-report

An isolated package directory can be supplied with --dependency-path PATH. --refresh-ekch --write-report regenerates only the combined EKCH example from current source data; it does not alter the fictional example or runtime YAML.

The report records two validated complete airport documents and 34 rejected invalid cases, including unknown/cross-handler settings, missing bays, invalid mappings/annotation types, ownership incompatibility, scripts/profile references, airport-local PDC logon/poller fields, missing selected region override/fallback files, unknown positions/routes, invalid resource paths, and session-owned feed caches. See the handler guide for runnable demonstrations, race checks, and benchmarks. Settings preservation and the tested handler decisions are separate claims; complete runtime parity remains integration work.

services:
  cdm:
    availability: deployment
    config_root: backend/config
    config:
      rate: 40
      rateLvo: 10
      rateUri: ekch/rate.txt
      sidIntervalUri: ekch/sidInterval.txt
      taxizonesUri: ekch/taxizones.txt
      defaultTaxiTime: 12
      deice:
        light: 3
        medium: 5
        heavy: 7
        super: 9
        platform:
        - name: A
          time: 5
        - name: B
          time: 6
        - name: V
          time: 10
  stand_assignment:
    availability: deployment
    stands:
      repo_path: backend/config/ekch/GRpluginStands.txt
    aircraft_reference:
      repo_path: backend/config/ekch/GRpluginAircraftInfo.txt
    aircraft_icao:
      environment: GRPLUGIN_ICAO_AIRCRAFT_JSON
      default_repo_path: backend/config/data/ICAO_Aircraft.json
    airline_assignment:
      repo_path: backend/config/ekch/airline_assignment.json
    scenery:
      repo_path: backend/config/ekch/gsx_sceneries.json
  text_pilot:
    availability: deployment
    provider: frequency-message/v1
    layout_data:
      repo_path: frontend/src/components/text-pilot/storyboard-layouts.json
  aman:
    availability: deployment
    terminal:
      repo_path: backend/config/aman/ekch-terminal-2611.json
    boundary:
      repo_path: backend/config/aman/boundaries/EKCH.json
  pdc:
    availability: deployment
    validation:
      heavy_runway_restriction:
        aircraft_types:
        - A388
        - B748
        - AN225
        allowed_runways:
        - 04R
        - 22L
      sid_restrictions:
      - sid: NEXEN
        engine_types:
        - J
      - sid: LANGO
        engine_types:
        - J
      - sid: KOPEX
        engine_types:
        - P
        - T
      - sid: BETUD
        engine_types: []
  ecfmp:
    availability: deployment
validation:
  clearance:
    sid_first_waypoints:
    - BETUD
    - GOLGA
    - KEMAX
    - KOPEX
    - LANGO
    - NEXEN
    - ODDON
    - ODON
    - SALLO
    - SALO
    - SIMEG
    - VEDAR
    sid_engine_rules:
    - code: sid_aircraft_type
      sid_families:
      - KOPEX
      disallowed_engine_types:
      - J
      message: Aircraft planned on SID not valid for ATYP. {recommendation}
      recommendations:
        MICOS: Reclear on NEXEN T503 MICOS... as filed
        ALS: Reclear on LANGO P999 AMRAK... as filed
        ALASA: Reclear on LANGO M611 ALASA... as filed
      default_recommendation: Reclear on Either NEXEN or LANGO DCT as filed.
    - code: sid_aircraft_type
      sid_families:
      - LANGO
      - NEXEN
      disallowed_engine_types:
      - P
      - T
      message: Aircraft planned on SID not valid for ATYP. {recommendation}
      recommendations:
        MICOS: Reclear on NEXEN T503 MICOS... as filed
        ALS: Reclear on LANGO P999 AMRAK... as filed
        ALASA: Reclear on LANGO M611 ALASA... as filed
      default_recommendation: Reclear on LANGO DCT... as filed
    aircraft_runway_rules:
    - code: category_f_runway
      aircraft_types:
      - A388
      - B748
      restricted_runways:
      - 22R
      - 04L
      - '12'
      - '30'
      restricted_sid_suffixes:
      - B
      - C
      - D
      - E
      message: Planned RWY not available for aircraft Category (CAT F). Only 04R/22L approved
    rnav_rules:
      nil:
        code: rnav_nil
        message: Aircraft filed on SID without RNAV capability. Clear via RV or update RNAV capability
          to "1".
      insufficient:
        code: rnav_insufficient
        capabilities:
        - '5'
        - '10'
        message: Aircraft filed on SID with insufficient RNAV capability. Clear via RV or update RNAV
          capability to "1".
    route_conflict_rules:
    - code: route_lango_egpx
      sid_families:
      - LANGO
      route_tokens_any:
      - ARTEX
      - ELSAN
      - REKNA
      - ITSUX
      - SURAT
      - EVRAL
      - ROPAL
      - LARGA
      - TIPAN
      - UPGAS
      remark_tokens_any:
      - EGPX/
      message: LANGO not valid for flights to EGPX. Refile to ODDON.
      allow_override: true
    - code: route_vedar_ekdk
      sid_families:
      - VEDAR
      route_tokens_any:
      - AAL
      - ARTOR
      - AMSEV
      remark_tokens_any:
      - EKDK/
      message: VEDAR not valid for re-entering EKDK. Refile to GOLGA
      allow_override: true
    - code: route_betud
      sid_families:
      - BETUD
      always: true
      message: BETUD not valid for flight. Refile via SALLO (Or SIMEG if more appropriate).
    - code: route_simeg_sallo
      sid_families:
      - SIMEG
      route_tokens_any:
      - SALLO
      message: SIMEG not valid as SID, when SALLO is on FPL. Refile to SALLO
      allow_override: true
  taxiway_types:
    apron:
      categories:
        E:
        - L/Y
        - Y/L
        - K/J
        - K1
        F:
        - L/Y
        - Y/L
        - K/J
        - K1
        - C/22L
        - G2/30
        - A3
        - A4
        - A5
        - B2
        - C/30
        - A1
        - A2
        - E1
        - B4
    tower:
      categories:
        D:
        - C/22L
        E:
        - C/22L
        - G2/30
        - A3
        - A4
        - A5
        F:
        - B2
        - C/30
        - A1
        - A2

        - A4
        - A5
        - E1
        - B4
      aircraft_types:
        A359:
