11

Commands, observations, and concurrent editing

#

Every frontend mutation resolves its tab binding, own plugin membership, session, airport definition, and observer/read-only status before workflow validation. Never choose a sender using CID alone or use the master as a fallback. If the same CID has multiple compatible EuroScope instances, require an explicit instance binding when it is otherwise ambiguous; keep this choice out of the ordinary single-instance flow.

Reuse existing move/field-edit validation, strip versions, ordering conflicts, command/result handling, and observable failure behavior. Carry the explicit membership/session context through those paths and recheck current authority before dispatch. Serialize conflicting actions using the existing mechanisms; a shared ownership-free board still requires conflict handling.

D3 is settled: use EKCH's current move execution, visible placement, error handling, and reconciliation, adapted to RADIS's workflow/mappings and lack of ownership. Reuse MoveFrontendStrip and the associated ordering/publication patterns; do not add a new ES-confirmation gate, pending-move UI/state machine, or durable action framework as a prerequisite for this release. The existing flow's local update/publication is not proof of an ES acknowledgement. Preserve current validation/failure/rollback behavior where applicable.

Keep any already existing domain transaction handling, such as EKCH PDC's own clearance state. A database mutation and an ES write are not one transaction; handle failures through the current mechanisms and reconcile observations. Do not automatically replay uncertain writes after reconnect or change of master. The in-memory proof demonstrates the boundary but is not a replacement for the existing production error paths or a full parity check.

Observations do not re-run controller write effects. Coded observation handlers reconcile local state separately, preserving explicit placement where generic ground state is insufficient. This prevents write/echo loops and preserves the current EKCH safeguards against stale ground-state updates moving strips backwards. Each airport independently evaluates relevant observations; physical flight facts may legitimately affect both airport workflows, but no direct board mirroring is introduced.

Automatic domain-service work is a distinct origin, not an observation echo or an invented human action. Human work deferred through a service retains its own plugin binding and does not gain master fallback. For genuine automatic work, D4 permits the same session's master or the controller who has assumed the aircraft, using the existing appropriate resolver and availability/permission checks. Reuse current unavailable-executor behavior; do not introduce a new execution orchestration system. PDC remains disabled at EKBI/EKYT, so additional regional PDC automation is not part of this release.

12

Reusable services and runtime isolation

#

Use the same service implementations with explicit airport/session dependencies. Separate immutable airport data, reusable aircraft/navigation reference data, shared live VATSIM snapshots, and mutable operational state. Share read-only reference datasets and live source caches when valid; keep each airport's operational maps and timers separate.

"Shared" identifies implementation and resource ownership, not one mutable airport-global state bag. Application-owned clients, workers, feeds, and caches can serve many airports. Immutable domain data is keyed by airport definition; mutable calculations, requests, subscriptions, and timers remain partitioned by their appropriate airport/session/environment. Do not require a separate service object for every session or merge state merely because a service is a singleton.

Shared PDC transport and scoped clearance processing

The user confirms one shared PDC service and the same credentials for all airports. Keep HOPPIE_LOGON at deployment scope and construct the provider client/HTTP transport once per application process. Reuse the shared PDC worker, message parsing, send path, and Web PDC API. Airport handlers request this service through typed intents executed by the core; they do not create clients, own logon secrets, or start independent poll loops. Application startup/shutdown owns its lifetime, not a single airport membership.

Shared credentials do not require one airport identity. The current client accepts from/poll callsign separately from its logon, and the service currently uses the airport code as that callsign. Preserve distinct airport mailboxes unless an operational requirement changes that identity. One shared coordinator may issue separate polls for distinct mailboxes; it must not duplicate polling of the same mailbox for every session/tab. Bind each live mailbox unambiguously to its authorized LIVE airport session. Training and playback do not poll/send through the live mailbox.

Shared at application scope Scoped to airport/session
Hoppie logon, provider client, HTTP transport, polling coordination, parsing, shared transport health, Web PDC integration Per-airport enablement, validation and workflow policy; session clearance records, transaction correlation, timeout state, frontend updates, and permissions

services.pdc in a combined airport file contains only availability and its typed validation settings. There is no per-airport key, transport, or polling configuration. Existing deployment credentials remain outside repository files; the same configured key is used for each enabled airport. Sharing PDC does not make it mandatory at every airport. PDC and AMAN are explicitly disabled at EKBI/EKYT, with no committed activation date. Preserve existing EKCH behavior; new-airport PDC/AMAN activation and its additional integration can remain deferred.

Dispatch requests by the polled mailbox/departure airport and resolve responses against the owning clearance transaction/session. Preserve session-scoped keys for pending requests, acknowledgements, timeouts, retries, and idempotency; callsign alone is insufficient. Disabling one airport prevents its new work without stopping another airport's polling or cancelling its clearances. Pending transactions follow their defined completion/timeout policy. Shared credentials and transport health do not merge airport state or relax command authority.

External message/sequence allocation and correlation must follow the mailbox identity's lifetime across session turnover (E5); an internal session key alone does not make a reused provider response ID unambiguous.

Handle errors per mailbox so one airport failure does not abort processing for all remaining airports. A shared provider/key outage is a shared channel-health condition; retain the existing Web PDC availability behavior when Hoppie is not configured. No new runtime PDC implementation or credential changes are made by this proposal update. Current PDC validation still reads package-global airport settings, and polling returns early on a mailbox error; shared construction alone does not establish completed multi-airport behavior. Both paths require adaptation. Mailbox/session turnover and response/sequence reuse are E5 work for future additional-airport PDC activation, not an EKBI/EKYT release gate.

Shared VATSIM acquisition and session projections

Preserve the existing application-level VATSIM source assembly. The main v3 pilot/prefile feed and the transceiver endpoint are separate upstream feeds; each has one owned refresh pipeline/cache per backend process, not one per airport, session, service instance, plugin membership, or frontend tab.

Fetch, parse, normalize, and index a source generation once. Publish a read-only snapshot with its source timestamp and refresh health. A reconciliation batch uses one consistent generation across its session projections; ordinary snapshot reads do not perform network I/O. Reuse the existing snapshot/source interfaces and last-good-data behavior. Centralize any on-demand refresh used by identity lookups and coalesce concurrent refresh requests, rather than letting session/service fan-out multiply upstream calls.

SAT, AMAN, coverage, and other consumers read the same source. They may compute filtered airport views, materialize relevant fields on independent strips, and maintain scoped reconciliation progress. They must not clone the entire global cache for every session or mutate source records with ownership, board order, clearance, stand reservations, or other operational results. Shared indexes by callsign/CID/airport belong with the source where useful. Workflow source precedence still applies: a feed update must not take ownership of controller/EuroScope fields merely because the data is shared.

The current normalized main-feed snapshot contains pilots and prefiles. If controller staffing is needed beyond the existing EuroScope observations, extend shared acquisition/normalization for that evidence rather than assuming it is already in the flight snapshot or introducing a poller per airport. Transceiver evidence remains shared as it is today.

Source lifetime follows aggregate application demand. Preserve existing demand from LIVE sessions and other enabled consumers such as EFB; also account for connected LIVE control instances that need staffing/radio evidence to detect coverage returning while they have zero airport memberships. Removing one membership must not stop or clear a source still needed elsewhere. Training, playback, and synthetic sources remain separate from public LIVE data; sharing a source must not bypass environment isolation.

Refresh failure and snapshot age are shared source-health facts, not independent fetch failures per airport. Each consumer applies its configured freshness and readiness policy to that shared health. A stale VATSIM snapshot does not by itself disconnect a working own plugin or replace the established read-only rules. Session cleanup removes only that session's projections/runtime state; it does not evict the application feed cache.

This is shared acquisition within the current backend process. A future multi-process deployment may add one external ingestion service or shared cache; that deployment change is outside the initial proposal. There is no session-level duplication in either case.

Service ownership and lifecycle

Service/resource Shared ownership Scoped data/work and adaptation
VATSIM network/transceivers One acquisition/cache pipeline per endpoint per application process. Airport/session projections and coverage decisions use the same immutable generation. Source demand includes connected LIVE control instances with no memberships.
PDC Preserve one application service, provider client, deployment logon, polling coordinator, and Web API. Keep EKCH behavior; disabled at EKBI/EKYT. Further airport validation/mailbox activation is deferred; future mailbox turnover work is E5.
CDM Reuse domain code and the existing application client/key; share immutable reference inputs where appropriate. Seed each enabled airport's typed data instead of EKCH alone. Partition calculations, schedules, subscriptions, and LIVE-only publication state; do not create provider clients per membership.
Stand assignment Shared allocator implementation, aircraft/reference data, and VATSIM source. Airport stand/airline/scenery definitions and readiness; session/environment reservations, blocks, assignments, and expiry. Remove global mutable stand registries.
AMAN Preserve domain code, navigation/reference data, and shared observations. Keep EKCH behavior; disabled at EKBI/EKYT with no committed activation. Airport-specific terminals/planning remain reusable for future requests, not a requirement to activate AMAN now.
Text pilots Shared protocol/routing code and the controller's existing multiplexed plugin transport. Airport-specific coded view/phrase inputs and session/request correlation. Never reuse EKCH presets implicitly or replace the human own-plugin binding.
ECFMP Preserve the application external client/acquisition service. Airport enablement, filtered applicability, and scoped operational results; do not duplicate upstream acquisition in handlers.
Weather/ATIS observations Reuse the existing application weather acquisition path; share observations per station/airport. Session presentation and authoritative runway/mode state remain distinct from weather/ATIS parsing. Integrating the prototype must not add a poller per browser.

Shared transport readiness and scoped capability readiness are different. A provider-wide outage affects all consumers of that channel; an invalid airport parameter or isolated domain error must not shut down unrelated airports.

Register/deregister session state and subscriptions with shared services using the existing session lifecycle. Do not construct/destroy a provider client or global worker on every membership or browser subscription change. An airport losing a master does not immediately delete its board or recreate service data; existing expiry/reconciliation applies. A service failure at one airport must not silently disable another airport's enabled service. Readiness is capability-specific: do not report a whole airport writable for an action whose required service is unavailable.

13

Persistence and operational scope

#

Preserve existing session/strip/controller foreign-key boundaries. Add scoped controller lookup/listing and any necessary indexes instead of treating CID as a unique session selector. Memberships and master epochs can initially remain in the existing backend's live connection registry; after restart they are rebuilt from authenticated connections and full sync. Persist operational workflow fields, pending actions where needed, and the effective definition revision used by an active session.

Apply required state/configuration migrations during the offline deployment. Preserve existing EKCH data and semantics. If this release renames persisted bays or adds annotation data, include the specific migration; do not silently reinterpret state or build an online old/new handler compatibility engine.

Record metrics/log context for airport, environment/session, definition revision, membership generation, master transition, and command outcome. Keep high-cardinality request/instance identifiers in logs rather than unbounded metric labels. Explain coverage additions/removals using responsibility and radio evidence so operators can distinguish a coverage decision from a failed plugin connection.

14

Implementation epics

#

The implementation epic plan, drafted on 2026-11-02, turns the confirmed design into eight published epics with 41 child issues. Each defines scope, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and exclusions. The issue index links every issue and the native hierarchy/dependency graph; spec PR #972 contains this specification. Implementation remains open.

Epic Result Prerequisites GitHub
MA-01 — Combined airport registry Full production loading, typed definitions, explicit activation, and preserved EKCH settings. None #973
MA-02 — Coded workflows and EKCH Production handler/action contracts and the actual EKCH decision/execution paths. MA-01 #974
MA-03 — Plugin memberships One connection, independent airport roles/sync, and exact own-plugin routing. MA-01, MA-02 #975
MA-04 — Coverage and rejoin Configured responsibilities/radios drive takeover and automatic return. MA-03, MA-05 #976
MA-05 — Shared services Shared sources/clients with scoped CDM/stand/text-pilot state; existing EKCH PDC/AMAN preserved. MA-01, MA-02 #977
MA-06 — Frontend session binding Authorized per-tab discovery, selection/switching, and existing read-only behavior. MA-03 #978
MA-07 — Integrated RADIS The full agreed prototype feature set plus restoration, authoritative shared boards, and own-plugin effects. MA-02, MA-04, MA-05, MA-06 #979
MA-08 — Validation and offline activation Integrated acceptance, approved airport data, and coordinated backend/frontend/plugin deployment. MA-01–MA-07 plus airport activation gates #980

Start with MA-01/02, then run transport and service work in parallel. Coverage and frontend selection follow, then the integrated RADIS milestone and release acceptance. Prototype UI adaptation, airport-data collection, and MA-08 baseline/ acceptance preparation can start earlier against agreed contracts.

The plan maps D1–D5 and E1–E7 to accountable epics. PDC/AMAN activation at EKBI/EKYT, additional-airport PDC mailbox redesign, ENGM, dual-protocol support, online migration, and a new pending-action framework are outside this release. Use the existing no-controllers-online deployment process and preserve EKCH data/behavior.

Airport data gates activation rather than implementation with test fixtures. Do not enable an incomplete airport or deploy the fictional example. The full plan below contains individual epic scope and linked child issues; there are no invented dates, owners, or airport operating values.

Read all eight epics, linked child issues, acceptance criteria, and release gates

MA-01: Load combined airport definitions in production

Tracker: #973.

Outcome: the application resolves one immutable definition per configured airport from its single combined file. Startup configuration is no longer equivalent to mutating one current-airport global.

Scope: full typed Go loading/validation for the existing combined schema, explicit deployment file selection, handler/settings registration, resource resolution, and definition revision. Preserve existing domain configuration formats and the complete EKCH data migration. Keep the fictional airport as test data that is never activated by repository scanning.

MA-01 owns definition/settings decoding and registration metadata; MA-02 owns runtime handler implementations and production execution. Loader tests can register fictional handler/view descriptors only within their test registry; they do not require a fictional frontend or enable that airport in production.

Child issues:

  • MA-01.1: #981 — implement typed combined-file loading and compose existing domain validators; include strict unknown/missing-field handling and useful source errors.
  • MA-01.2: #982 — build the immutable registry and compiled handler/settings factory registration; validate known handler/view/bay references without a generic interpreter.
  • MA-01.3: #983 — resolve repository and environment-backed assets consistently, including region fallback/override behavior and disabled-service dependencies.
  • MA-01.4: #984 — connect application assembly to the complete EKCH definition and migrate current configuration consumers incrementally through explicit context.
  • MA-01.5: #985 — add full-loader/schema parity cases using EKCH and the fictional definition; replace reliance on the proof's partial YAML-node projection.

Acceptance:

  • The actual application loader consumes the combined EKCH file and preserves all 20 current YAML settings, 18 bays, master priorities, and relevant constants.
  • Two selected definitions coexist without changing each other's resolved data. An unknown airport/handler never falls back to EKCH.
  • Invalid selected definitions fail startup with airport/field/resource context; examples and unselected definitions are not silently activated.
  • Region environment overrides/defaults behave as authored; repository paths remain constrained, and required selected assets are checked.
  • Disabled regional PDC/AMAN do not require deployment data or start work. Existing EKCH service enablement/credentials remain deployment-controlled.
  • The registry is immutable after startup. Event handling does not parse YAML, load files, or search for a handler factory.

Not included: hot reload, an admin configuration editor, or guessing real EKBI/EKYT operating values. Traceability: E1 and the single-file/handler decision.

MA-02: Route workflows through coded handlers and preserve EKCH

Tracker: #974.

Outcome: production workflow decisions depend on the session's bound handler and typed definition. EKCH's rules remain real tested code, with shared execution and guard mechanisms rather than scattered airport conditionals.

Scope: production handler/action descriptors, pure decisions, scoped context, and execution through existing database, ordering, EuroScope, and domain-service operations. The existing sample is reference code, not the final SDK or executor.

Child issues:

  • MA-02.1: #986 — define the minimal production hooks for controller actions, normalized observations, admission/lifecycle, and coordination; register typed supported actions with handlers instead of growing the sample core allowlist.
  • MA-02.2: #987 — put existing EKCH bay/reconciliation, lifecycle, ownership, and special coordination behavior behind its handler, including SQ resolution. Supply settings/geography from the definition rather than hidden constants.
  • MA-02.3: #988 — adapt existing move/field-edit executors to explicit session, definition, and source authority; retain EKCH validation, ordering, errors, rollback, and observation reconciliation.
  • MA-02.4: #989 — keep human own-plugin binding separate from genuine automatic master/assuming-controller resolution, using existing appropriate helpers.
  • MA-02.5: #990 — exercise EKCH full and incremental observation paths, movement, completion/removal, and coordination with production stores or faithful fixtures. Retain a fictional custom handler test proving a feature needs no core airport branch.

Acceptance:

  • EKCH's specific taxi placement, solo-tower promotion, departure progression, clearance/ownership checks, handoffs, and removal behavior retain their meaning. Test both full sync and incremental updates, not only the two sample hooks.
  • The common dispatcher selects a bound implementation; a handler change does not require adding an airport switch or every custom action to the common core.
  • Controller edits, including work passed through a shared service, retain their own binding. Missing/disconnected bindings never fall back to the master.
  • Genuine automatic effects resolve an available authorized executor in the same session, using master or assuming controller as appropriate.
  • Handlers own no database/provider client, polling loop, or mutable current airport. Validate decisions before mutation and perform network I/O outside session/strip locks and transactions.
  • Preserve current concurrency and move/error behavior. No new confirmation gate, pending-move UI, outbox, or durable action engine is required.

Not included: a declarative rule language or full production equivalence inferred from the existing sample tests. Traceability: D3, D4, E2, E3.

MA-03: Support independent airport memberships over one plugin connection

Tracker: #975.

Outcome: one authenticated EuroScope instance participates in multiple sessions, with independent roles, synchronization, and command routing.

Child issues:

  • MA-03.1: #991 — update the existing protobuf envelopes/control messages with the required instance, membership, session/environment, generation, and master context. Upgrade both ends together; do not build a parallel legacy endpoint.
  • MA-03.2: #992 — split backend transport identity from logical membership clients; replace global/CID-only role, observer, disconnect, and sender assumptions.
  • MA-03.3: #993 — replace the plugin's singular role/session state with a membership map, scoped full-sync inventories, removal tracking, and role state. Collect callbacks once and dispatch under the applicable membership roles.
  • MA-03.4: #994 — elect and synchronize masters independently, including stale-source fencing at application time and non-master controller command/result handling.
  • MA-03.5: #995 — retain identity/radio/control updates when zero memberships remain; expose authorized membership discovery for the frontend and coverage coordinator.

Acceptance:

  • The same plugin can be master for two airports and non-master for another; a role or full-sync change in one cannot reset or delete another's state.
  • Human commands route to the exact initiating compatible instance/membership, not a CID-wide lookup or whichever plugin is master.
  • Reconnect, late messages, old master snapshots, and membership removal cannot write through stale or wrong-session contexts.
  • Removing one membership retains the transport and unaffected memberships; zero-membership control updates remain available without keeping operational controller rows or session cleanup artificially alive.
  • LIVE, Sweatbox, and playback identities remain isolated. Existing startup delay, reconnect, and disconnect behavior are retained.

Not included: distributed election, online failover, simultaneous old/new protocols, or a new generic acknowledgement protocol. Traceability: D4, D5, E3.

MA-04: Coordinate airport coverage, takeover, and automatic rejoin

Tracker: #976.

Outcome: memberships follow responsibilities and radios even when a controller has no active airport membership. Coverage remains independent of strip ownership.

Child issues:

  • MA-04.1: #996 — evaluate enabled definitions against server-authorized eligibility, configured responsibilities/providers, primary identity, and tuned frequencies.
  • MA-04.2: #997 — assemble normalized staffing/radio evidence from shared providers, including controllers without FlightStrips; extend shared staffing acquisition if necessary rather than assume the current pilot/prefile snapshot contains it.
  • MA-04.3: #998 — apply desired-membership deltas and the confirmed bounded takeover rule, preserving unaffected memberships and independent mastership.
  • MA-04.4: #999 — handle evidence freshness/unknown states explicitly using existing matching behavior as the baseline; test radio changes without callsign changes.
  • MA-04.5: #1000 — connect automatic rejoin, zero-membership source demand, and existing offline/read-only transitions without creating a new disconnected workflow.

Acceptance:

  • When only EKBI_TWR is online, an EKDK instance retains configured approach participation. APP taking over all remaining responsibilities removes it.
  • Relinquish at replacement backend attachment or the bounded configured grace, whichever comes first, including an absent/delayed replacement plugin. Respect the intentional plugin startup delay; do not repurpose it as the grace period.
  • When APP leaves, a still-connected eligible EKDK instance rejoins automatically, including from zero memberships, and synchronizes before editing.
  • Tuned-frequency changes affect coverage without requiring a callsign change. RADIS participation does not require sector/strip ownership.
  • No polling loop or full staffing/radio cache is created per membership. LIVE evidence does not leak into exercise/playback sessions.

Activation inputs: actual airport roles/frequencies/providers/master values, regions, and grace value. Synthetic fixtures unblock implementation. Traceability: E4 and the confirmed takeover/rejoin requirements.

MA-05: Isolate airport service state while sharing sources and clients

Tracker: #977.

Outcome: enabling another airport does not duplicate global acquisition or external clients and does not reuse EKCH's mutable airport settings/state.

Child issues:

  • MA-05.1: #1001 — preserve shared VATSIM/transceiver sources, indexes, last-good-data, and refresh coordination; include aggregate demand from zero-membership LIVE control instances alongside existing service/EFB consumers.
  • MA-05.2: #1002 — seed CDM from each enabled airport's definition/data and partition calculations, schedules, subscriptions, and LIVE-only publication state.
  • MA-05.3: #1003 — replace implicit EKCH/global stand registries with airport-specific stand/airline/scenery definitions and scoped reservations/assignments/expiry; keep read-only aircraft/reference inputs shared where appropriate.
  • MA-05.4: #1004 — supply airport-specific text-pilot presets/actions through existing transport and own-plugin routing. Adapt weather/ATIS presentation to shared backend acquisition instead of browser-local polling.
  • MA-05.5: #1005 — preserve application-owned CDM/PDC/ECFMP clients, the shared PDC logon/worker, and current EKCH PDC/AMAN. Ensure other airport definitions cannot overwrite EKCH validation/configuration. Enforce regional PDC/AMAN disablement in server APIs, service registration, polling, and publication paths, not just frontend capabilities; skip disabled regional PDC mailboxes even when the application-level client remains enabled for EKCH.
  • MA-05.6: #1006 — attach/detach scoped work on existing session lifecycle without transferring ownership of global clients/workers to memberships or browser tabs.

Acceptance:

  • Source/client/worker construction and upstream request counts demonstrate application ownership while multiple airports, sessions, and tabs are active. Distinct upstream endpoints/mailboxes may still require distinct requests.
  • CDM and stand state/data do not leak between airports, LIVE, and exercises. No unconfigured airport silently loads EKCH rates/stands/presets.
  • Source failure/age is shared health; consumers retain their existing scoped readiness behavior. One session cleanup cannot clear another's source or work.
  • Human text-pilot/service edits retain the own-plugin binding, and genuine automatic work uses an eligible same-session executor under D4.
  • Existing EKCH PDC/AMAN remain operational. Regional PDC/AMAN are disabled and do not demand assets, mailboxes, workers, or new-airport activation work. Direct regional requests cannot bypass disablement through the shared service.

Not included: additional-airport PDC reply/sequence redesign (future E5), regional AMAN, or a fork of existing domain services. Traceability: D2, D4, shared-source/PDC requirements, E1/E4/E6.

MA-06: Bind each frontend tab to an authorized airport session

Tracker: #978.

Outcome: each tab shows and edits its selected authorized board, with clear own-plugin readiness and no cross-tab or cross-airport store contamination.

Child issues:

  • MA-06.1: #1007 — replace singular CID/controller association with authorized membership/session discovery, scoped observer/readiness/capability data, and explicit instance selection only when multiple compatible own instances exist.
  • MA-06.2: #1008 — implement one-eligible auto-entry, multiple-eligible initial chooser, airport switcher, and independent per-tab selection/store state.
  • MA-06.3: #1009 — bind the board WebSocket and initial snapshot to the selected session, definition revision, coded view, action catalog, and capabilities.
  • MA-06.4: #1010 — reject delayed traffic/results after switching/rebinding and retain the selected board read-only through own-plugin loss and normal reconnect.

Acceptance:

  • One eligible session enters directly; several show a choice; none retains the current no-plugin behavior. Discovery never chooses an arbitrary CID row.
  • Two tabs can show different airports without one tab changing the other's selection. Switching does not change plugin membership or mastership.
  • Server authorization and binding checks protect mutations, not only UI hiding. Old subscriptions/results cannot mutate a newly selected airport.
  • A disconnected own plugin keeps the current board read-only even if another master remains connected. Existing observer restrictions apply per membership.

Not included: several simultaneous boards in one tab or compatibility with an old frontend during rollout. Traceability: D5, E3 and navigation requirements.

MA-07: Deliver the integrated RADIS board for EKBI/EKYT

Tracker: #979.

Outcome: adapt the reviewed PR #958 prototype into the host application as a shared coded view/handler, with independent authoritative boards and actual controller-plugin effects.

Child issues:

  • MA-07.1: #1011 — inventory current prototype features, fields, menus, and dialogs; map each implemented interaction to a typed backend action and acceptance case. Distinguish working controls from placeholders without inventing new capabilities.
  • MA-07.2: #1012 — implement the RADIS handler/settings/schema and authoritative bay/order/annotation/lifecycle storage using the required specific migrations. Include all four observed containers and ownership-free collaboration.
  • MA-07.3: #1013 — adapt board/strip components, menus, runway/SID/route/heading, squawk/altitude, VFR/RNAV, stand, notes, de-icing, and REA/ATA controls to host stores, styles, backend actions, and existing plugin execution/results.
  • MA-07.4: #1014 — implement shared NEW local-strip creation and FIND connected-pilot lookup/admission, with stable strip identity and duplicate prevention. Never create an ES flight plan or add prefiles/unrelated airport flights.
  • MA-07.5: #1015 — implement automatic appearance/removal plus manual removal and restoration, shared hidden/recovery state, and refresh/restart reconciliation that preserves explicit placement and controller annotations.

Acceptance:

  • Every current implemented prototype feature has a production action/test or operational acceptance case; notes, de-icing marks, REA/ATA, and restoration are included. Explicit NEW/FIND and PDC/AMAN decisions override demo shortcuts.
  • Two non-observer participants see the same bay/order/field/annotation/removal changes with concurrency checks and reconnect/restart convergence. No ownership is required and no airport-local operation directly mirrors to another airport.
  • Human bay/field edits use their bound own plugin and current EKCH execution/ error patterns. All edits, including annotations, NEW, delete, and restore, remain blocked under the agreed disconnected read-only policy.
  • NEW creates a shared local strip only; ES-dependent actions require a valid associated flight context. FIND searches only connected pilots to/from the selected airport using the shared source; no prefiles or demo ten-flight cap.
  • Manual deletion survives refresh and is restorable according to the configured policy. Restore does not duplicate identity or delete/replace the ES flight plan.
  • EKBI/EKYT have independent definitions and state while reusing RADIS code. There is no standalone second app, browser VATSIM polling, or duplicate stand allocator. PDC/AMAN stay disabled.

Activation inputs: actual bay/ES and field mappings, appearance/removal values, recovery limits, timestamp semantics, and service/airport data. Do not copy ENGM's recovery duration, REA/EOBT assumptions, or prototype thresholds as defaults. Traceability: D1–D4, E2/E3/E6 and the prototype/reference notes.

MA-08: Validate and activate the release in an offline window

Tracker: #980.

Outcome: demonstrate the complete agreed release across backend, frontend, plugin, and operational airport definitions, then deploy it using the normal offline process without disturbing existing EKCH behavior.

Child issues:

  • MA-08.1: #1017 — establish the release acceptance matrix and capture existing EKCH workflow/service behavior and representative load before the refactor; keep this evidence current while MA-01–MA-07 progress.
  • MA-08.2: #1018 — run production-loader, database, protocol/plugin, browser, and service integration scenarios spanning independent airports/environments; prove no cross-session routing and no duplicated shared acquisition/client lifetime.
  • MA-08.3: #1019 — collect and validate real EKBI/EKYT files, service datasets, mappings/thresholds, and named operational acceptance. Keep fictional fixtures distinct from selected deployment files.
  • MA-08.4: #1020 — compare representative EKCH and concurrent-airport performance, locks/queues, shared-source requests, and service behavior. Set practical regression/load acceptance from these measurements, not the sample microbenchmarks.
  • MA-08.5: #1021 — document and rehearse the existing deployment/migration/smoke process; verify nobody is online, update backend/frontend/plugin together, and enable only airports whose configuration and acceptance are complete.

Acceptance:

  • All scoped architecture scenarios pass with the actual production paths, including independent sync/master epochs, takeover/return from zero memberships, tuned-radio changes, multi-tab switching, non-master own-plugin edits, concurrent RADIS work, restoration, and LIVE/exercise/playback isolation.
  • Existing EKCH moves, routing, service behavior, observer/offline/reconnect, and persisted state retain their operational meaning; actual relevant service and plugin regression evidence is attached, not just the sample helper tests.
  • Each activated regional airport has approved concrete data and the full RADIS feature matrix, with CDM/stands/text pilot available and PDC/AMAN disabled.
  • Backend restart/session cleanup and service health preserve scoped state and shared resource ownership using existing failure/recovery mechanisms.
  • A coordinated no-controllers-online deployment updates the components and required data/migrations together. Normal deployment failure/rollback procedures are used; no online migration or legacy-client support layer is introduced.
  • The release evidence states the measured workload/results and any accepted remaining limitations. Disabled or incomplete airport activation is explicit.

Not included: making future multi-airport PDC acceptance scenarios or ENGM activation release blockers. Traceability: D5, E6/E7 and all initial-release architecture acceptance scenarios.

The existing isolated proof and Astra's architecture verdict support the plan but do not replace this implementation evidence.

Acceptance scenarios

#

Architecture checks can use explicitly synthetic configurations; operating values are not invented to make those fixtures production airport definitions.

Scenario Required outcome
EKDK participates in EKCH and EKYT. Independent views, strips, master roles, sync readiness, and command bindings.
One plugin is master for two airports and non-master for a third. Role changes and full sync in one membership do not change the others.
EKBI_APP takes over from EKDK, with delayed or absent plugin attachment. EKDK relinquishes at attachment or the configured grace deadline; existing read-only behavior covers any readiness gap.
Only EKBI_TWR is online below EKDK. EKDK retains approach participation as configured.
APP leaves after EKDK has no active memberships. The control connection receives coverage changes and EKDK rejoins automatically.
Radio tuning changes without a callsign change. Coverage and membership are reevaluated using tuned-frequency evidence.
More airports, sessions, service consumers, or browser tabs use VATSIM data. One fetch/parse/cache pipeline per upstream feed remains at application scope; snapshot reads do not create additional upstream requests or full session-local cache copies.
One shared feed generation serves EKBI and EKYT. Consumers derive independent airport state from the same immutable generation; one session's edits/cleanup cannot mutate or evict the shared source.
Future additional-airport PDC activation (deferred, not an initial-release gate). One service/provider client and deployment logon serve distinct airport mailboxes; validation, clearance state, responses, and timers remain session-scoped.
Future additional-airport PDC mailbox turnover/disablement (deferred). Poll each authorized LIVE mailbox once per coordinator cycle; no duplicate session pollers, cross-session acknowledgements, or interruption of other airports' work.
The last active membership leaves but a LIVE EKDK control instance is waiting for coverage to return. Shared staffing/radio acquisition remains available while demanded, allowing automatic reattachment without a session-owned poller.
VATSIM refresh fails while other data and own plugins remain connected. Consumers see the same source age/error and apply scoped readiness policy; the existing own-plugin/offline behavior is not globally replaced.
Two RADIS controllers edit or reorder the same board. Shared result with concurrency conflict handling, no ownership requirement, no cross-airport changes.
RADIS notes, de-icing marks, or timestamps change and a second controller reconnects. Both see the persisted session-strip annotations; annotation writes do not implicitly amend ES fields and are blocked by the agreed disconnected read-only policy.
Source records arrive in a different order or a hidden strip reappears in a feed snapshot. Backend strip identity stays stable and shared visibility/removal policy is preserved.
A controller uses RADIS NEW. Create a shared airport-local strip only; actual ES flight-plan creation is deferred. The strip is not evidence of an ES acknowledgement, and ordinary readiness/observer restrictions apply.
A controller uses RADIS FIND. Search only connected pilots whose flight origin or destination matches the selected airport; exclude prefiles. Selecting a flight does not imply ES flight-plan creation.
RADIS annotations and manually removed strips. All current prototype annotation controls are included, and users can restore manually removed strips; values/mappings and recovery limits are supplied for the airport.
RADIS move/error handling and automatic effects. Follow existing EKCH execution/error/reconciliation patterns. Human writes use their own plugin; genuine automatic effects can use the same session master or assuming controller.
EKBI/EKYT service activation. CDM, stand assignment, and text-pilot support form the delivery set; PDC and AMAN remain disabled, without changing EKCH activation.
A non-master controller changes squawk or moves a strip. Exactly its bound own plugin receives the command. Disconnect blocks edits even if another master remains available.
A flight goes from EKBI to EKYT. Independent strip placement/order; flight-plan observations converge through ES without copying bay operations or issuing the command twice.
A tab switches airports while an old result is in flight. Old binding traffic cannot mutate the new board or execute a pending action there.
A master disconnects during full sync. Stale epoch traffic cannot overwrite the replacement; incomplete sync cannot remove unrelated flights.
LIVE, Sweatbox, and playback use the same airport/callsign. No mixed discovery, writes, mastership, service output, or cleanup.
Invalid handler/settings, missing data, or disabled service. Explicit airport/service diagnosis; no implicit EKCH defaults.
Coordinated deployment with no controllers online. Backend, frontend, plugin, and required migrations update together. EKCH data/behavior and reconnect semantics are preserved without concurrent legacy/new client support.
Backend restart or uncertain ES action. Reuse existing scoped state/sync and error/reconciliation behavior; do not introduce automatic replay of uncertain mutations.
16

Alternatives and consequences

#
Alternative Assessment
One backend/deployment per airport Leaves the controller/plugin association and switching problems unresolved and duplicates operations. Prefer one airport-aware backend with existing deployment constraints.
One session containing several airports Conflicts with independent strip/board state and expands the migration of already-session-scoped data. Preserve airport sessions.
One EuroScope socket per airport Reuses current framing but duplicates authentication, reconnect, observation/sync machinery, and still needs a control path to restore an absent membership. Multiplexing is preferred despite the explicit protocol migration.
Multiplex frontend boards within each tab Adds store/routing complexity without a current product requirement. Use one board subscription per tab.
Global strip/flight store as the first migration Adds authority and synchronization questions beyond this delivery. Keep per-session rows and existing ES authority.
A fork of the backend/services for every airport Duplicates common behavior and creates drift. Share the core and services; support distinct coded workflow handlers where behavior differs.
Every airport behavior encoded in YAML Turns configuration into an expanding programming language. Prefer registered coded handlers with concrete typed settings and shared helpers.
General scripting engine or configuration-rendered UI Larger scope than required, with harder validation and compatibility. Use bounded backend configuration and coded views.

The proposed approach adds membership/protocol complexity and requires careful audits of global/CID-wide state. In return, it preserves existing session boundaries and working offline behavior while allowing genuinely different airport workflows. ENGM remains representable without making RADIS as complex as EKCH or requiring every airport to have ownership.

The user resolved D1–D5 on 2026-11-01. The planning register records the confirmed outcomes and supersedes the earlier open recommendations. The proposal now maps to eight planned implementation epics. Their scope is recorded in this repo and all 49 issues are published; runtime integration is not complete.

ID Confirmed decision
D1 All current RADIS prototype features/controls, notes/de-icing/REA/ATA annotations, and restoration of manually deleted strips. NEW is shared local-strip creation only; FIND is connected pilots flying to/from the selected airport, without prefiles.

Keep E1–E7 as proportionate engineering work: production config loading, typed handler/action contracts, necessary session/identity/concurrency context, coverage evidence, specific state migrations, and representative performance checks. There is no remaining product decision in this register that needs to be answered before drafting epics.

They may stay open during epic planning. ENGM remains a future design input, not a first release target. No invented prototype constants become airport defaults.

Reviewed on 2026-10-30 against the architecture, configuration requirements, schema/semantic validator, both combined examples, executable handler proof, reference notes, and relevant application assembly/command/PDC code.

Decision update — 2026-11-01: the user has resolved D1–D5. The proposal is ready to turn into implementation epics with the confirmed scope below. Airport operating values remain rollout inputs; engineering details belong in the work. The 2026-10-30 audit remains useful evidence, with its findings updated below. The review itself creates no runtime activation or deployment. The subsequent implementation plan is now published as eight epics and 41 child issues with native hierarchy/dependency links; see the issue index and spec PR #972. The epic plan was prepared after the independent architecture review below.

Independent final review: 2026-11-02

An Astra sub-agent independently reviewed the proposal, supporting documents, schema/examples, handler proof, and relevant production code. No architecture or epic-planning blockers remain. The confirmed D1–D5 decisions are consistent; documented proof limits and E1–E7 implementation work are not reopened decisions.

The review found one P2 authoring-tool defect: the schema allowed environment-backed region files, but the semantic validator assumed repo_path and raised a KeyError. The validator now supports both declared resource forms, honors an explicit environment override, uses the default for unset/blank values, and reports missing selected files as validation errors. Focused checks were added. Astra verified the correction and closed the finding.

Final validation preserves both combined examples and all 20 EKCH settings, rejects 34 invalid cases, and checks region-resource resolution. This independent review does not claim full runtime integration, EKCH parity, or production performance validation; those remain the explicitly scoped implementation work.

Settled requirements carried forward

  • Compiled workflow handlers with concrete typed settings; one combined file per airport, with large domain assets referenced rather than copied.
  • Shared RADIS implementation/view for EKBI/EKYT where behavior matches; independent airport boards, strips, order, and session/environment state.
  • No RADIS strip/sector ownership. Writable non-observer participants use their own plugin for controller-initiated edits. Disconnected boards stay read-only.
  • Independent configurable coverage/master policy, tuned-radio consideration, bounded relinquishment on takeover, automatic rejoin, and existing offline behavior. The already agreed takeover timing is not reopened here.
  • Shared VATSIM/transceiver acquisition and caches; shared application PDC service, provider client, logon, and polling coordination. Configuration, permissions, clearance state, and operational results keep explicit scope.
  • Coded frontend views, one selected session per tab, airport switching, and an initial chooser only when multiple eligible sessions exist.
  • Repository configuration/restart deployment. New handler/view code is expected; no general rule interpreter, runtime script system, or code-free onboarding.

Inconsistencies corrected or made explicit

Finding Resolution in the proposal
Requirements still described a declarative transition model and old discovery text said handler selection was pending. Replaced the current model with coded decisions/settings and marked the discovery chronology as historical. General handler selection exists in the example schema; production integration remains future work.
The overview and membership diagrams could imply a service instance/client per session. Show shared application services explicitly; sessions own partitions of operational state, not duplicate global clients/workers.
The text described handlers invoking services, while the proof returns pure decisions. Handler decisions describe typed core/domain operations; the executor invokes services outside the decision's critical section. Handlers own no I/O, worker, transport, or mutable current-airport state.
The proposal required waiting for ES confirmation before moving a bay, while the sample commits immediately. Identified the sample's immediate in-memory commit as a proof limit and recorded D3: use the current EKCH move/error/reconciliation behavior. No new ES-confirmation gate or pending-move framework is required.
Own-plugin routing for human edits was stated too broadly for automatic PDC work. Keep the human rule fixed. D4 now permits genuine automatic work through the session master or controller who has assumed the aircraft. Retain the exact own-plugin binding for human-originated work.
PDC could appear ready for multiple airports because its client is already shared. Distinguish existing shared transport from remaining work: validation still reads global config, current polling returns on an airport error, and mailbox/session handover needs response-correlation work if PDC is later activated at additional airports. PDC stays disabled at EKBI/EKYT now.
Full-file schema validation could be confused with a complete production Go loader. State that Python checks the complete documents; the Go proof strictly decodes only the workflow projection and selected context. Schema/Go parity is implementation work, not proven by two valid fixtures.
The proof could imply a complete extensible action dispatcher or admission model. Its core still knows the two sample command kinds, indexes strips by callsign, and bypasses production admission. Those limitations are explicit; production needs handler action descriptors, stable strip identity, and admission/lifecycle hooks.
Benchmarks could be interpreted as a no-regression guarantee. Retain them as historical in-memory measurements. Representative EKCH baseline/load and production acceptance budgets remain engineering work.
Broad first-release service reuse and deferred airport parameters were mixed together. D1/D2 now fix the first release: current RADIS prototype features plus restoration; PDC and AMAN disabled at EKBI/EKYT, with no scheduled activation.

Confirmed delivery decisions

Resolved by the user on 2026-11-01. These supersede the recommendations from the initial audit and should be copied into affected epic scope/acceptance criteria.

D1 — First RADIS feature boundary: resolved

  • Include all current prototype features and editing/menu controls, with the already agreed integrated shared-board/own-plugin behavior. A feature in the demo is not permission to retain browser-only state or feed-only writes.
  • Include notes, de-icing marks, and REA/ATA timestamps.
  • Include restoration of manually deleted strips in the first release. Recovery limits and detailed airport mappings remain rollout/handler inputs.
  • NEW creates a shared airport-local strip only. ES flight-plan creation is deferred. Creation itself is not an ES acknowledgement; ordinary readiness and observer restrictions still apply.
  • FIND includes connected pilots only, whose flight origin or destination is the selected airport. Prefiles and unrelated flights are excluded.

All current features refers to the reviewed RADIS prototype baseline, not every EKCH/ENGM feature. The explicit PDC/AMAN exclusion in D2 still applies. Detailed field semantics and values must be supplied without silently broadening NEW or FIND. The prototype review records limitations and incomplete controls.

D2 — First-release service rollout: resolved

Plan EKBI/EKYT with CDM, stand assignment, and text-pilot support. PDC and AMAN are disabled there, with no committed activation date; the user expects AMAN may remain disabled for a long time. Do not make new-airport activation or a complete multi-airport PDC/AMAN migration a prerequisite for RADIS delivery.

Preserve current EKCH services. PDC remains a shared application service/client, logon, and polling coordinator wherever enabled. New airport settings remain scoped so introducing RADIS does not disturb EKCH. Additional PDC mailbox or AMAN activation work can be planned only when those capabilities are requested.

D3 — Board behavior during ES operations: resolved

Use what EKCH does today for move execution, visible placement, validation, error handling, and reconciliation, adapted to RADIS's own handler/mappings and lack of ownership. Reuse the current production move flow rather than introduce an additional acknowledgement gate, pending-move UI/state machine, or durable action framework for this release.

The relevant current paths are frontend moves, move execution, and ordering/publication. Preserve existing error/rollback behavior where applicable. Neither queue acceptance nor the in-memory proof is an ES acknowledgement or full parity test.

D4 — Automatic service authority: resolved

Genuinely automatic work may use the session master or the controller who has assumed the aircraft, via the existing appropriate service/aircraft executor resolution. The chosen plugin must belong to the same session and be available and authorized for that operation. Retain current failure/unavailable-executor behavior rather than invent a new service-execution system.

Human-originated edits, including work deferred through a service, still use that human's own bound plugin. Do not relabel a human request as automatic to use master fallback. PDC is disabled at EKBI/EKYT; preserve existing EKCH PDC behavior rather than make new-airport automatic PDC integration a release gate.

D5 — Deployment and compatibility: resolved

Deploy in a window when no controllers are online, updating the backend, frontend, and plugin together. The user does not require concurrent legacy/new client support. Remove dual-protocol endpoints, legacy-client adapters, and a long compatibility window from this delivery plan.

Keep the new session-aware protocol internally coherent and verify that everyone is offline before applying the deployment/migrations. Offline rollout does not remove the need for correct reconnect/session isolation after deployment or preservation of EKCH data/behavior. Use the existing deployment process; no new rollout orchestration or online failover system is required.

Engineering decisions to resolve within the relevant epics

These are scoped implementation details, not unresolved product questions or prerequisites for drafting epics. Keep them proportionate to the existing code and the agreed offline deployment; use the existing mechanisms where possible.

ID Decision/work and recommended direction Must be resolved before
E1 Production registry activation/loading and validation. Use an explicit deployment list of airport files, never auto-activate examples by scanning the repo. Recommend atomic validation of selected definitions before startup; reuse the existing offline deployment/failure process. Compose full domain validators, enforce exact handler settings and supported views, and test schema/Go parity. Production registry integration/activation.
E2 Production handler/action/effect contract. Register typed supported actions with each handler instead of extending the proof's core command allowlist. Specify pure decisions, service requests, lifecycle/coordination hooks, and typed contracts. Follow the existing EKCH execution/error path and persist using current concurrency mechanisms; do not perform network I/O while holding strip/session locks or transactions. Migrating real actions/services behind the boundary.
E3 Protocol identity, source precedence, and concurrency. Define membership/master epochs, request/result correlation, board-order conflict handling, stable strip/incarnation identity and optional flight association. The same callsign can be reused or refer to an airport-local strip. Feed observations must not overwrite higher-authority ES/controller facts. Protocol/persistence implementation.
E4 Coverage evidence precedence and freshness. Distinguish unknown/stale staffing or radios from a confirmed takeover/absence. Recommend preserving an established membership on transient unknown evidence while reevaluating, without overriding the agreed deadline after a confirmed takeover. Define simulation-source isolation and the zero-membership demand path. Coverage coordinator behavior tests.
E5 Deferred PDC mailbox/session handover and external reply correlation when another airport is enabled. One coordinator owns a LIVE mailbox; persist/identify outstanding transactions across session turnover. Session-local sequence IDs alone may be ambiguous externally after reuse. Correlate mailbox, aircraft, external response ID, and owning transaction; reject/hold ambiguous replies. Ensure one mailbox error does not stop the rest. Future additional-airport PDC activation; not an EKBI/EKYT release gate.
E6 Persisted state, handler versions, config revision, and disablement. Preserve EKCH state in the offline migration and define the required new fields. Reuse existing cleanup/service-state handling; do not build an online old/new compatibility layer. Removing a membership or tab does not own global service lifetime; disabling an airport does not delete state or authorize reinterpreting it as EKCH. Offline migration/restart and per-airport disablement acceptance.
E7 Performance acceptance and observability. Measure representative EKCH before/after behavior with simultaneous airports, controller/timer/feed workloads, and slow external services. Agree regression/load budgets from those measurements; the sample's sub-microsecond dispatch is not the budget. Count shared workers/requests and keep locks scoped. Production performance acceptance, not epic drafting.

Airport rollout inputs that may remain open during epic planning

Input Required before
Coverage responsibilities, tuned-frequency/position lists, master priorities, grace value, and relevant regions Activating that airport's participation policy.
Runways/procedures, allowed actions, bay-to-ES mappings, arrival/departure/local handling, admission/removal/recovery thresholds Operational acceptance of that airport's handler.

Evidence and practical limits

The schema report records two combined configs, lossless preservation of all 20 EKCH YAML settings, and 34 rejected invalid inputs. The Go proof tests handler binding, the actual EKCH bay helper paths, custom fictional behavior, isolated sessions/config, guards, revision conflicts, and snapshots. Race checks include that package and the existing shared bay helpers.

Neither suite tests real multi-airport membership, WebSockets, database transactions, service integration, ES acknowledgement, persisted restart, controller-feed freshness, or production performance. No test should be described as full EKCH migration/parity or RADIS operational validation.

Useful application evidence: shared service assembly, PDC client, PDC service/automatic routing, current global PDC validation, strip concurrency queries, and existing bay reconciliation.

The epic descriptions should link these confirmed D1–D5 outcomes and the relevant engineering items, separating delivery acceptance from airport-data gates. The eight published epics now assign this work. No further product decision in this register blocks planning; actual airport values and operational acceptance are still required before activation.
